### Picard: portrait panel

For a phone or an upright tablet: a [header bar](lcars-design#header-bar-with-a-title) with the title, code blocks beside a condition readout, a tile wall, a gauge bank, toggle tabs and a segmented closing bar. Recorded at 600 by 1000.

<video class="doc-video" src="/gallery/picard-portrait.webm" poster="/gallery/picard-portrait.webp" title="Picard portrait: a red MISSION OPS header bar, code blocks beside a condition readout, three framed number tiles, three vertical gauges and three toggle tabs" autoplay loop muted playsinline></video>

::: details YAML
```yaml
# Picard portrait: the "portrait panel" archetype from doc/getting-started/lcars-design.md,
# for a phone or an upright wall tablet. A header bar with the title, a condition readout
# beside a column of code blocks, a tile wall, a gauge bank, toggle tabs and a segmented
# closing bar. Every colour is a theme role. Uses lcards_test_* helpers.
title: Picard Portrait
views:
  - title: Portrait
    path: portrait
    type: custom:lcards-layout-view
    layout:
      height: calc(100dvh - var(--header-height, 56px))
      padding: 10px
      grid-gap: 8px
      grid-template-columns: 120px minmax(0, 1fr)
      grid-template-rows: 56px 150px 120px minmax(0, 1fr) 52px 40px
      grid-template-areas: |
        "title  title"
        "codes  status"
        "tiles  tiles"
        "gauges gauges"
        "tabs   tabs"
        "foot   foot"
    cards:
      # Header bar with the title.
      - type: custom:lcards-button
        view_layout:
          grid-area: title
        preset: bar-label-left
        text:
          label:
            content: MISSION OPS
            color: theme:colors.ui.tertiary
        style:
          card:
            color:
              background:
                default: theme:colors.ui.tertiary

      # Code blocks, two of them tied to helpers.
      - type: custom:lcards-layout-card
        view_layout:
          grid-area: codes
        layout:
          grid-gap: 6px
          grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr)
          grid-template-rows: repeat(4, minmax(0, 1fr))
        cards:
          - { type: custom:lcards-button, preset: panel-light, min_height: 0, text: { label: { content: 07-82, position: center-right } } }
          - type: custom:lcards-button
            preset: panel-light
            min_height: 0
            entity: input_boolean.lcards_test_lights
            text: { label: { content: 75-15, position: center-right } }
            tap_action: { action: toggle }
          - { type: custom:lcards-button, preset: panel-dark, min_height: 0, text: { label: { content: 7-385, position: center-right } } }
          - type: custom:lcards-button
            preset: panel-light
            min_height: 0
            entity: input_boolean.lcards_test_doors
            text: { label: { content: 19-587, position: center-right } }
            tap_action: { action: toggle }

      # Condition readout.
      - type: custom:lcards-data-grid
        view_layout:
          grid-area: status
        data_mode: data
        rows:
          - values: [CONDITION, "{{ 'NORMAL' if states('input_number.lcards_test_shields') | int > 30 else 'ALERT' }}"]
          - [POWER, "{{ states('input_number.lcards_test_power') | int }} %"]
          - [SHIELDS, "{{ states('input_number.lcards_test_shields') | int }} %"]
        grid:
          grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr
          grid-template-rows: repeat(3, min-content)
          gap: 6px
        style:
          font_size: 20px
        columns:
          - style:
              align: left
              color: theme:colors.ui.primary
          - style:
              align: right
              color: theme:colors.ui.tertiary

      # Tile wall.
      - type: custom:lcards-layout-card
        view_layout:
          grid-area: tiles
        layout:
          grid-gap: 8px
          grid-template-columns: repeat(3, minmax(0, 1fr))
          grid-template-rows: minmax(0, 1fr)
        cards:
          - type: custom:lcards-elbow
            elbow:
              type: frame
              segment: { color: theme:colors.card.topColor }
              frame: { bar_width: 3, bar_height: 3, outer_curve: 8 }
            symbiont:
              enabled: true
              position: { top: 8, right: 8, bottom: 8, left: 8 }
              imprint: { enabled: false }
              card:
                type: custom:lcards-data-grid
                data_mode: decorative
                format: digit
                grid:
                  grid-template-rows: repeat(3, auto)
                  grid-template-columns: repeat(2, minmax(0, 1fr))
          - type: custom:lcards-elbow
            elbow:
              type: frame
              segment: { color: theme:colors.ui.tertiary }
              frame: { bar_width: 3, bar_height: 3, outer_curve: 8 }
            symbiont:
              enabled: true
              position: { top: 8, right: 8, bottom: 8, left: 8 }
              imprint: { enabled: false }
              card:
                type: custom:lcards-data-grid
                data_mode: decorative
                format: hex
                grid:
                  grid-template-rows: repeat(3, auto)
                  grid-template-columns: repeat(2, minmax(0, 1fr))
          - type: custom:lcards-elbow
            elbow:
              type: frame
              segment: { color: theme:colors.card.topColor }
              frame: { bar_width: 3, bar_height: 3, outer_curve: 8 }
            symbiont:
              enabled: true
              position: { top: 8, right: 8, bottom: 8, left: 8 }
              imprint: { enabled: false }
              card:
                type: custom:lcards-data-grid
                data_mode: decorative
                format: float
                grid:
                  grid-template-rows: repeat(3, auto)
                  grid-template-columns: repeat(2, minmax(0, 1fr))

      # Gauge bank.
      - type: custom:lcards-layout-card
        view_layout:
          grid-area: gauges
        layout:
          grid-gap: 8px
          grid-template-columns: repeat(3, minmax(0, 1fr))
          grid-template-rows: minmax(0, 1fr)
        cards:
          - { type: custom:lcards-slider, component: picard, preset: picard-gauge-vertical, entity: input_number.lcards_test_power }
          - { type: custom:lcards-slider, component: picard, preset: picard-gauge-vertical, entity: input_number.lcards_test_shields }
          - { type: custom:lcards-slider, component: picard, preset: picard-gauge-vertical, entity: input_number.lcards_test_humidity }

      # Toggle tabs.
      - type: custom:lcards-layout-card
        view_layout:
          grid-area: tabs
        layout:
          grid-gap: 6px
          grid-template-columns: repeat(3, minmax(0, 1fr))
          grid-template-rows: minmax(0, 1fr)
        cards:
          - type: custom:lcards-button
            preset: toggle-tab
            entity: input_boolean.lcards_test_lights
            text: { name: { content: LIGHTS } }
            tap_action: { action: toggle }
          - type: custom:lcards-button
            preset: toggle-tab
            entity: input_boolean.lcards_test_doors
            text: { name: { content: DOORS } }
            tap_action: { action: toggle }
          - type: custom:lcards-button
            preset: toggle-tab
            entity: input_boolean.lcards_test_toggle
            text: { name: { content: AUX } }
            tap_action: { action: toggle }

      # A segmented bar closes the panel (no sweep: nothing below for it to turn into).
      - type: custom:lcards-layout-card
        view_layout:
          grid-area: foot
        layout:
          grid-gap: 6px
          grid-template-columns: 120px 3fr 1fr 2fr
          grid-template-rows: 16px
```

### Classic: sweep console

The classic look: thick header and footer sweeps continued as [labelled segments](lcars-design#segmented-bar-classic-arms), a sidebar of coloured blocks with code numbers, a [pill grid](lcars-design#pill-grid-classic) led by big numbers, a slider over a strip of small pills, and a number cascade. The view sets `theme: LCARS Default`, so the roles come out in the TNG pastels whatever your profile theme is.

<video class="doc-video" src="/gallery/tng-console.webm" poster="/gallery/tng-console.webp" title="TNG console: peach header sweep and blocks, rows of pastel pills led by large numbers, two control bars, a pill slider and a column of blue numbers" autoplay loop muted playsinline></video>

::: details YAML
```yaml
# TNG console: the classic look from the patterns in doc/getting-started/lcars-design.md.

# segments, a sidebar of blocks with code numbers, a pill grid led by big numbers in
# alternating roles, a slider and a strip of small pills, a number cascade. Every colour
# is a theme role, and the view uses the LCARS Default theme, so the roles come out in
# the classic pastels. Uses lcards_test_* helpers.
title: TNG Console
views:
  - title: Operations
    path: operations
    theme: LCARS Default
    type: custom:lcards-layout-view
    layout:
      height: calc(100dvh - var(--header-height, 56px))

      grid-gap: 6px
      grid-template-columns: 170px 110px minmax(0, 3fr) minmax(0, 2fr)
      grid-template-rows: 56px 64px minmax(0, 1fr) 150px 70px
      grid-template-areas: |
        "corner corner bar    bar"
        "corner corner title  title"
        "side   pills  pills  readout"
        "side   status status readout"
        "fcorner fcorner fbar fbar"

      # Header: a short thick sweep, the bar continued as labelled segments in several roles.

          grid-area: side
        layout:
          grid-gap: 6px
          grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr)
          grid-template-rows: 2fr 1fr 1fr 3fr 1fr
        cards:
          - type: custom:lcards-button
            preset: panel-light
            min_height: 0
            text: { label: { content: 01-23564 } }
          - type: custom:lcards-button
            preset: panel-light
            min_height: 0
            text: { label: { content: 02-24156 } }
            style: { card: { color: { background: { default: theme:colors.ui.secondary } } } }

            preset: panel-light
            min_height: 0
            text: { label: { content: 03-41248 } }
            style: { card: { color: { background: { default: theme:colors.ui.tertiary } } } }
          - type: custom:lcards-button
            preset: panel-light
            min_height: 0

            style: { card: { color: { background: { default: theme:colors.card.topColor } } } }
          - type: custom:lcards-button
            preset: panel-light
            min_height: 0
            text: { label: { content: 05-32456 } }
```

### Classic: bracket screen

DS9-style: top and bottom bars broken into labelled segments, a sidebar of coloured blocks with code numbers, a shuttlecraft cutaway in colour, a readout list and a row of pills. The view uses `theme: LCARS Zeldaar`.

<video class="doc-video" src="/gallery/ds9-bracket.webm" poster="/gallery/ds9-bracket.webp" title="DS9 bracket: violet top and bottom sweeps, a sidebar of violet, peach, rose and blue blocks, a colourful shuttlecraft cutaway, a system status list and a row of pills" autoplay loop muted playsinline></video>

::: details YAML
```yaml
# DS9 bracket: the "bracket screen" archetype from doc/getting-started/lcars-design.md.
# A top and a bottom bar (short sweeps continued as labelled segments) with the title, a sidebar of blocks with code numbers, a
# cutaway display, a side readout list and a row of pills under the display. The view
# uses the LCARS Zeldaar theme for a DS9 palette; every colour is a theme role.
# Uses lcards_test_* helpers.
title: DS9 Bracket
views:
  - title: Runabout
    path: runabout
    theme: LCARS Zeldaar
    type: custom:lcards-layout-view
    layout:
      height: calc(100dvh - var(--header-height, 56px))
      padding: 12px
      grid-gap: 8px
      grid-template-columns: 150px 110px minmax(0, 3fr) minmax(0, 1fr)
      grid-template-rows: 70px minmax(0, 1fr) 64px 70px
      grid-template-areas: |
        "tcorner tcorner tbar    tbar"
        "side    display display list"
        "side    pills   pills   list"
        "bcorner bcorner bbar    bbar"
    cards:
      # Top bar: a short sweep continued as segments, the title under them.
      - type: custom:lcards-elbow
        view_layout:
          grid-area: tcorner
        elbow:
          type: header-left
```

### Classic: list

Voyager-style: a [split header](lcars-design#split-header-classic) whose two bars continue as segments, a number cascade, a duty roster [list](lcars-design#list), a column of big numbers and pill groups. The view uses `theme: LCARS Nemesis Blue`.

<video class="doc-video" src="/gallery/voyager-roster.webm" poster="/gallery/voyager-roster.webp" title="Voyager roster: a tan upper sweep and a blue lower sweep, a duty roster in four coloured columns, a column of large numbers, a number cascade and a row of pills" autoplay loop muted playsinline></video>

::: details YAML
```yaml

# header (an upper block sweeping down into a bar, a lower one sweeping out of the next),
# a number cascade in the header, a roster list, a column of big numbers and a row of
# pill groups. The view uses the LCARS Nemesis Blue theme; every colour is a theme role.
# Uses lcards_test_* helpers.

  - title: Roster
    path: roster
    theme: LCARS Nemesis Blue
    type: custom:lcards-layout-view
    layout:
      height: calc(100dvh - var(--header-height, 56px))

      grid-gap: 8px
      grid-template-columns: 160px 100px minmax(0, 1fr) 260px
      grid-template-rows: 150px 50px minmax(0, 1fr) 70px

        "ucorner ucorner upper   cascade"
        "lcorner lcorner lower   lower"

      # Split header: the upper block sweeps down into a bar continued as segments...
      - type: custom:lcards-elbow

          type: footer-left

            bar_height: 20

      - type: custom:lcards-layout-card
        view_layout:
          grid-area: upper
        layout:
          grid-gap: 6px
          grid-template-columns: 3fr 1fr 2fr
          grid-template-rows: minmax(0, 1fr) 20px
          grid-template-areas: |
            "title title title"
            "s1 s2 s3"
        cards:
          - type: custom:lcards-button
            view_layout: { grid-area: title }
            preset: text-only
            min_height: 0
            text: { label: { content: "VOYAGER DUTY ROSTER · 12.25.95", show: true, position: center-right, font_size: 32, color: theme:colors.ui.tertiary } }
          - { type: custom:lcards-button, preset: panel-light, min_height: 20, view_layout: { grid-area: s1 }, text: { label: { content: "CREW ASSIGNMENTS", position: center-right } }, style: { card: { color: { background: { default: theme:colors.ui.secondary } } } } }
          - { type: custom:lcards-button, preset: panel-light, min_height: 20, view_layout: { grid-area: s2 }, text: { label: { content: "47", position: center-right } }, style: { card: { color: { background: { default: theme:colors.ui.tertiary } } } } }
          - { type: custom:lcards-button, preset: panel-light, min_height: 20, view_layout: { grid-area: s3 }, text: { label: { content: "DECK 5", position: center-right } }, style: { card: { color: { background: { default: theme:colors.ui.primary } } } } }

          grid-template-rows: repeat(5, auto)
          grid-template-columns: repeat(4, minmax(0, 1fr))
          gap: 0px
        style:
          padding: 0px
          font_size: 18px
        animations:
          - trigger: on_load
            preset: cascade-color
      # ...and the lower one sweeps out of the next, also continued as segments.
      - type: custom:lcards-elbow
        view_layout:
          grid-area: lcorner
        elbow:
          type: header-left
          segment:
            bar_width: 160
            bar_height: 20
            color: theme:colors.ui.primary
      - type: custom:lcards-layout-card
        view_layout:
          grid-area: lower
        layout:
          grid-gap: 6px
          grid-template-columns: 1fr 4fr 1fr 2fr
          grid-template-rows: 20px
        cards:
          - { type: custom:lcards-button, preset: panel-light, min_height: 20, text: { label: { content: "02-262000", position: center-right } }, style: { card: { color: { background: { default: theme:colors.ui.primary } } } } }
```

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/getting-started/getting-help.html -->

# Getting Help

Something not working? Work through these in order: most problems are a config typo or a setup issue, and both are quick to rule out.

## 1. Check your config

Paste your card YAML (or the whole dashboard) into **[Check Your Config](config-checker)**. It finds options that don't exist, misspelt preset, animation and colour names, and values of the wrong kind, each with the line and a suggestion. Fix what it reports first: a config LCARdS doesn't understand is silently ignored, which often looks like a bug.

Using Claude with the [LCARdS skill](ai-assistance#with-claude-easiest)? Paste the YAML and ask it to check and fix it.

## 2. Run the health check

Open the **LCARdS** sidebar panel → **Welcome** tab → **Support & system info**.

The checklist covers the most common causes of problems:

| Check | What it means |
|---|---|
| **Home Assistant version** | LCARdS requires Home Assistant **2026.10** or newer. |
| **Frontend = integration version** | If these differ, your browser is running a cached copy of an older LCARdS. Hard-refresh (Ctrl+Shift+R / Cmd+Shift+R), or clear the companion app's frontend cache. If you just updated, restart Home Assistant. |
| **UI eXtension (UIX) / card-mod** | HA-LCARS styles Home Assistant through [UIX](https://github.com/Lint-Free-Technology/uix). **card-mod** no longer works with current Home Assistant and conflicts with UIX. Uninstall it in HACS and remove its `extra_module_url` line from `configuration.yaml`. |
| **card-mod in `extra_module_url`** | A leftover `frontend: extra_module_url` entry still loads card-mod. Remove it and restart. |
| **custom:layout-card** | Shown when `custom:layout-card` is installed. LCARdS cards can shrink inside it; switch to the LCARdS [Layout Card](../cards/layout-card/). |
| **Lovelace resources** | LCARdS loads itself through the integration. An old manually added resource (e.g. `/hacsfiles/lcards/lcards.js`) or a duplicate loads it twice. Remove extras under **Settings → Dashboards → ⋮ → Resources**. |
| **HA-LCARS theme** | Shows whether an HA-LCARS theme is active. LCARdS works without it, but it is designed to pair with it. |

Resource and `extra_module_url` checks need an **admin** user.

## 3. Common problems

- **Cards collapse or margins look wrong inside `custom:layout-card`:** use LCARdS's own [Layout Card](../cards/layout-card/) instead. Change the `type` to `custom:lcards-layout-card` and remove `layout_type`; the rest of the config stays the same. See [Sizing inside `custom:layout-card`](../cards/common#sizing-inside-custom-layout-card).
- **Cards look out of date after an update:** hard-refresh the page (Ctrl+Shift+R / Cmd+Shift+R) or clear the companion app's frontend cache.
- **Styling from card-mod stops working:** card-mod no longer works with current Home Assistant; HA-LCARS uses [UIX](https://github.com/Lint-Free-Technology/uix) instead. Remove card-mod.
- **Moving over from CB-LCARS?** See [Coming from CB-LCARS](cb-lcars-migration) for the equivalent of each card.

## 4. Report an issue

Still stuck? In the same section:

- **Report an issue** opens a GitHub bug report with your LCARdS version, Home Assistant version and support info already filled in. It also copies the full info to your clipboard. Review the form, describe the problem, add your card YAML, then submit. Nothing is sent automatically.
- **Copy support info** copies the same information, to paste into an existing issue or a [Discussion](https://github.com/snootched/LCARdS/discussions).
- Tick **Include data-source names & entity IDs** only if the problem involves data sources.

Expand **Preview what will be shared** to see exactly what is included. That means versions, browser, theme, UIX/card-mod status, integration options and the most recent LCARdS warnings. Those warnings can mention entity names, so review before sharing.

::: tip Please use the template
Issues need the bug report template so we have the versions and environment we need. Issues opened without it are labelled `needs-template`. Edit the issue to add the template sections, or use **Report an issue**.
:::

## Other ways to collect info

**Download diagnostics**, Home Assistant's standard diagnostics file:
**Settings → Devices & services → LCARdS → ⋮ → Download diagnostics**. It contains the same backend facts plus Home Assistant's own system information.

**Browser console** (F12 → Console):

```javascript
window.lcards.info()                    // quick summary
await window.lcards.support.copy()      // copy full support info to the clipboard
await window.lcards.support.openIssue() // copy + open a pre-filled bug report
await window.lcards.support.collect()   // raw support data (object)
```

Pass `{ includeConfig: true }` to the `support.*` calls to include data-source names and entity IDs.

---

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/getting-started/installation.html -->

# Installation

## Requirements

- **Home Assistant 2026.10 or newer.** LCARdS relies on 2026.10's dashboard visibility handling and validation library; on older versions the integration logs an error and does not load.

Something not working after installing? See [Getting Help](getting-help.md); the LCARdS panel's Welcome tab has a built-in health check.

## Quick Start

1. [Install from HACS](#_1-install-via-hacs)
2. [Add the LCARdS integration](#_2-add-the-integration)
3. [First setup in the LCARdS panel](#_3-first-setup): create the helpers, then tune alert modes and sounds

:::tip HA-LCARS Theme Integration
LCARdS supports and integrates well with [**HA-LCARS themes**](https://github.com/th3jesta/ha-lcars).  Use these two together for the best experience.

HA-LCARS includes LCARdS theme profiles (**LCARS Picard [LCARdS Red Accent]** and **[LCARdS Blue Accent]**): choose one as your Home Assistant theme and HA's own screens match your LCARdS cards. See [HA-LCARS Theme Profiles](../configuration/ha-lcars-theme-profiles.md).
:::

## 1. Install via HACS

[![Open in HACS](https://my.home-assistant.io/badges/hacs_repository.svg)](https://my.home-assistant.io/redirect/hacs_repository/?owner=snootched&repository=LCARdS&category=integration)

1. Open **HACS** in Home Assistant
2. Go to **Integrations** and search for **LCARdS**
3. Click **Download** and confirm
4. **Restart Home Assistant**, then [add the integration](#_2-add-the-integration).

### Manual Installation

<details><summary>Manual installation (unmanaged updates)</summary>

1. Download `lcards.zip` from the [latest GitHub release](https://github.com/snootched/lcards/releases/latest)
2. Extract the contents into `config/custom_components/lcards/`
   (the directory should contain `manifest.json` and `__init__.py` directly, not a nested `lcards/lcards/` folder)
3. **Restart Home Assistant**, then [add the integration](#_2-add-the-integration).

</details>

::: info Using `custom:layout-card`?
LCARdS has its own [Layout Card](../cards/layout-card/), which fixes the sizing and margin problems LCARdS cards have inside `custom:layout-card` and adds a visual editor. Moving over is a one-line change: see [Sizing inside `custom:layout-card`](../cards/common#sizing-inside-custom-layout-card).
:::

## 2. Add the integration

Go to **Settings > Devices & services > Add integration** and pick **LCARdS**. The integration adds the **LCARdS Config** panel to the sidebar and loads the cards on every dashboard. Its options are listed under [Integration options](#integration-options).

## 3. First setup

Open **LCARdS Config** in the sidebar. The **Welcome** tab walks you through the same steps:

1. **Create the helpers.** In the **Helpers** tab, click **Create All Helpers**. LCARdS keeps alert mode, sound and sizing settings in Home Assistant helpers, and several features (alert mode, the alert overlay, sounds) need them. Do this first.
2. **Pick your alert colours** (optional). The **Alert Mode Lab** in **Theme Studio** sets how each alert mode recolours your dashboards. See [Alert Mode Lab](../configuration/alert-mode-lab).
3. **Set up sounds** (optional). The **Sounds** tab turns sounds on, picks a sound scheme and sets volumes. See [Sound Configuration](../configuration/sounds).
4. **Choose your HA-LCARS theme** (recommended), ideally one of the LCARdS profiles HA-LCARS includes. See [HA-LCARS Theme Profiles](../configuration/ha-lcars-theme-profiles).

Then check the setup: **Welcome > Support & system info** runs a health check (versions, browser cache, card-mod leftovers).

The [Configuration](../configuration/) section covers every panel tab in detail.

## Next steps

- **[Build a dashboard](building-dashboards)**: pick cards and lay out your first LCARS screen.
- **[Browse the gallery](dashboard-gallery)**: start from a complete dashboard.
- Stuck? See **[Getting Help](getting-help)**.

## Integration options

**Settings > Devices & services > LCARdS > Configure**. Changes take effect immediately; no restart needed.

| Option | Default | Description |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| Show sidebar panel | On | Display the LCARdS Config entry in the Home Assistant sidebar. Disable if you prefer a cleaner sidebar; the integration stays active and all cards continue to work. |
| Sidebar Title | LCARdS Config | Customizable title for the sidebar entry. |
| Sidebar Icon | `mdi:space-invaders` | Customizable icon for the sidebar entry. |
| Log Level | `warn` | Default logging level for all cards. `debug`, `trace` are very verbose: only use them for deep troubleshooting. |
| Enable Preview Features | `false` | Unlocks features that are still under active development. These may change during development - Please provide your feedback, discuss or get help on GitHub Issues and Discussions. |

If you don't want the panel in the sidebar all the time, turn **Show sidebar panel** off; it can be turned back on at any time.

---

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/getting-started/lcars-design.html -->

# Designing LCARS Screens

What makes a screen read as LCARS, written down as guidelines you can pick from. They come from studying the screens people recognise: the *Star Trek: Picard* season 3 consoles (as rebuilt by meWho's Titan.DS and LCARSlad London) and production panels from *The Next Generation*, *Deep Space Nine* and *Voyager*.

None of this is required. A dashboard that follows three of these guidelines already looks more like LCARS than one that follows none; pick the ones that suit your screen. [Building a Dashboard](building-dashboards) covers the mechanics (which card for which job, the layout view); this page is about the look.

## Two looks

| | Picard (Titan.DS, *Picard* S3) | Classic (TNG, DS9, Voyager) |
|---|---|---|
| Structure | Thin frames in a few dark, muted tones | Thick blocks of colour |
| Colour | Mostly black and structure tones; a little accent | Several pastel colours at once |
| Buttons | Small square blocks with code numbers, pills at the edges | Grids of rounded pills, led by big numbers |
| Main display | Line-drawn schematic inside a nested frame | Content inside a bracket or sweep frame |
| Themes that suit it | `LCARS Picard [LCARdS Red/Blue Accent]`, `LCARS Picard I/II`, `LCARS 25C` | `LCARS Default`, `LCARS TNG`, `LCARS Classic`, `LCARS Nemesis Blue` |

Most of the guidelines below apply to both. The look mostly comes from the theme: the same layout reads as Picard in a Picard theme and as TNG in a classic one.

## Colour comes from your theme

Don't pick colours for an LCARS screen; pick **roles**, and let the theme supply the colour. Then the screen follows when you switch themes, into light or dark mode, and into alert mode.

| Role | Use for | Token | HA-LCARS variable |
|---|---|---|---|
| Main structure | Sweeps, frame bars, the most important frame | `theme:colors.ui.primary` | `--lcars-ui-primary` |
| Secondary structure | Block columns, side bars | `theme:colors.ui.secondary`, `theme:colors.ui.quaternary` | `--lcars-ui-secondary`, `--lcars-ui-quaternary` |
| Dark structure | Inner frames, inactive blocks, tabs | `theme:colors.card.topColor`, `theme:colors.card.bottomColor` | `--lcars-card-top-color`, `--lcars-card-bottom-color` |
| Accent | What's on, selected or needs attention | `theme:colors.ui.tertiary`, `theme:colors.card.buttonOn` | `--lcars-ui-tertiary`, `--lcars-card-button-color` |
| Data | Readings, schematic lines, gauges | | a palette colour, e.g. `var(--lcars-blue, var(--lcards-blue-medium))` |
| Alert | Alert states | | `var(--lcars-alert-color, var(--lcards-orange-dark))` |
| Text on a role | Labels on a coloured block | | the role's text partner: `--lcars-ui-primary-text`, `--lcars-card-top-text`, ... |

**Prefer the `theme:` tokens.** They resolve to your [HA-LCARS](https://github.com/th3jesta/ha-lcars) theme's variable when it's installed and fall back to the LCARdS palette when it isn't, so the card always has a colour. A bare `var(--lcars-...)` is empty without HA-LCARS: give it a fallback, as in the table. HA-LCARS themes have one accent role, so the data colour is a deliberate pick from the palette: check it reads on your theme's structure colours.

- **Keep accent colour sparse.** In the Picard references only about a tenth of the screen is accent colour; the rest is black and structure tones. A block stays a structure colour unless it means something.
- **Classic screens are more colourful**: several roles side by side, mixed freely. The classic themes already set their roles to the pastel set.
- **Light and dark mode belong to the theme.** If your theme has both, a screen built from roles works in both.
- **A view can choose its own theme**: `theme: LCARS Default` on a view shows that view in that theme, whatever the user's profile theme is. Handy for a classic screen on an otherwise Picard dashboard.

## Structure

- **Black canvas.** Content sits on black inside frames, not on coloured blocks.
- **Sweeps make the frames.** A frame is a bar that turns 90° into another bar (an [elbow](../cards/elbow/)). Two sweeps facing each other (a header pair, or a left and a right sweep) is the signature LCARS shape; a lone elbow in a corner is rarer.
- **Nest frames.** Put a thinner frame inside the main one around the most important content. Picard screens nest two thin frames; classic ones put a thin sweep inside a thick one.
- **Break long bars into segments** of different lengths, separated by small black gaps. A segment can carry a small label or number.
- **One gap size everywhere.** The same gap between blocks, segments and frames on a screen (`grid-gap` on the layout view and layout cards). Blocks never touch.
- **Labels sit right-aligned**, usually at the bottom right of their block, in condensed capitals (the theme font). Numbers right-aligned in columns.
- **One title, top right**, large, in the accent colour or white; a dim subtitle at the bottom right if you need one. Classic titles often read `NAME • NUMBER`.
- **Numbers as texture.** Code-like numbers (`13-650`, `0099•06`) fill blocks and columns, and dense number cascades fill spare areas. Real readings and decorative numbers look alike; that's part of the look.
- **A sweep is at least as wide as what it frames.** If a sweep's vertical bar is narrower than the column above it, it looks detached; close a narrow column with a segmented bar instead.
- **Fill space with structure, not black.** If an area is empty, put blocks, a number cascade or a segmented bar in it.

## Picard

- **Columns of small number blocks** down one or both sides: mostly structure tones, a few in the accent, some dark (inactive). See [code-block column](#code-block-column).
- **A utility column of small dark pills, housed inside a bracket frame** at the far edge (zoom, settings, dimmer), with a red alert pill at the bottom. See [utility pills](#utility-pills).
- **Concentric sweeps**: a thick sweep with a thin line running parallel inside it, for headers and corners. See [concentric sweep](#concentric-sweep).
- **Controls inside a wide arm**: a thick frame whose black inset holds a group of blocks. See [controls inside a wide arm](#controls-inside-a-wide-arm).
- **Vertical gauges with tick scales** beside the number columns ([Picard and gauge sliders](../cards/slider-card/)).
- **The main display is a schematic**: a line drawing with leader lines to labels, small accent highlights for faults ([MSD](../cards/msd/)).
- **A strip of tabs and sliders along the bottom.** Tabs show their state as a line along the top ([`toggle-tab`](#toggle-tab-strip)).
- **Fixed chrome, changing centre.** Titan.DS keeps the same frame, columns and strips on every screen and swaps only the central display. In LCARdS: a layout view whose centre area holds several cards with [visibility conditions](../cards/layout-view/), one shown at a time.

## Classic (TNG, DS9, Voyager)

- **Colour blocks are the structure.** Thick header blocks, often in several roles side by side.
- **Grids of rounded pills**, each with a small code label, in column groups that alternate two or three roles. See [pill grid](#pill-grid-classic).
- **A column of big numbers** (`20`, `008`, `358`) leads each group of pills.
- **Bracket frames**: a top and a bottom bar with rounded ends, and a sidebar of stacked blocks with code numbers. See [bracket frame](#bracket-frame-classic).
- **A split header**: two sweeps meeting across the top, with a thin segmented band in the gap between them.
- **Segment the long arms.** A classic bar seldom runs unbroken across the screen: the sweep turns into a short bar, then segments of different lengths and roles carry labels. See [segmented bar](#segmented-bar-classic-arms).

## Motion and alerts

- **At rest, move small things only**: ticking numbers, a dot row, a scanning line. On the reference screens about one twentieth of the screen moves at a time. [Animations](../core/animations.md), [data grid cascades](../cards/data-grid/).
- **Animate entrances once** (`on_show` with `draw`, `cascade` or `text-reveal`), not continuously.
- **Alerts change the whole screen at once**: [alert mode](../core/alert-mode.md) recolours everything in place, and an [alert overlay](../cards/alert-overlay/) adds the alert symbol. Avoid making every card flash.
- **Show state by colour in place**, not by moving things: a block turns to the accent, a tab's line lights up.

## Screen archetypes

Start a screen by picking its overall shape, then fill the areas with [patterns](#patterns). These are the layouts that recur across the reference screens; each one suits a different job. Mix them: a Picard screen can use the wings layout, a classic one the tile wall. Take groupings and sections from the [gallery](dashboard-gallery) and the references freely, but compose the screen for its own job rather than reproducing one whole.

| Archetype | Good for | Shape (`grid-template-areas`) | In the gallery |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Display with side columns** | One main system (a ship, a floor plan, a chart) with controls around it; Titan.DS modules | `"pills top top top" "pills left main right" "pills left strip right"` | [Picard](dashboard-gallery#picard-display-with-side-columns) |
| **Display over controls** | A wide display with a dense control deck under it; Titan.DS ship screens | `"head head" "display display" "deck1 deck2"` | [Picard](dashboard-gallery#picard-display-over-controls) |
| **Wings** | Two related halves (port and starboard, upstairs and downstairs) around a shared centre | `"head head head" "lwing centre rwing"` |  |
| **Portrait panel** | Phones and wall tablets mounted upright | `"title" "main" "gauges" "controls"` | [Picard](dashboard-gallery#picard-portrait-panel) |
| **Tile wall** | Many similar things at once: cameras, rooms, sensors | `"head head head" "t1 t2 t3" "t4 t5 t6"` |  |
| **Sweep console** | A classic control panel: thick header sweep, sidebar, button groups | `"head head head" "side pills readout" "foot foot foot"` | [Classic](dashboard-gallery#classic-sweep-console) |
| **Bracket screen** | A readout or a document: capped top and bottom bars, a numbered sidebar | `"top top" "side main" "bottom bottom"` | [Classic](dashboard-gallery#classic-bracket-screen) |
| **List** | Rosters, schedules, logs: rows of text under a split header | `"head head" "list numbers" "pills pills"` | [Classic](dashboard-gallery#classic-list) |

Two things vary a screen more than anything else: which archetype you start from, and which patterns you put in its areas. A screen that reuses one gallery screen's grid with new labels is the same screen; one that combines a different archetype with two or three patterns is a new one.

## Patterns

Building blocks to compose a screen from. Each is a [layout card](../cards/layout-card/) you can drop into a layout view area, with every colour from a theme role. Change the numbers, labels and entities to yours.

Two things keep a pattern from collapsing when you change it: give the layout card's rows a size (`grid-template-rows` or `grid-auto-rows` in px or `minmax(0, 1fr)`; rows left to size themselves squash the cards), and keep a button's row at least as tall as the button (56 px by default; small pills and blocks set a lower `min_height`, bar labels size their text to it).

### Code-block column

The Picard side column: small blocks with code numbers, mostly structure, one in the accent.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-layout-card
layout:
  height: 300px
  grid-gap: 6px
  grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr
  grid-auto-rows: minmax(0, 1fr)
cards:
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: panel-light
    min_height: 28
    text: { label: { content: 63-934, position: center-right } }
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: panel-light
    min_height: 28
    text: { label: { content: 13-650, position: center-right } }
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: panel-light
    min_height: 28
    text: { label: { content: 19-638, position: center-right } }
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: panel-light
    min_height: 28
    entity: light.demo
    text: { label: { content: 42-991, position: center-right } }
    tap_action: { action: toggle }
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: panel-light
    min_height: 28
    text: { label: { content: 28-130, position: center-right } }
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: panel-light
    min_height: 28
    text: { label: { content: 50-957, position: center-right } }
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: panel-light
    min_height: 28
    text: { label: { content: 81-782, position: center-right } }
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: panel-light
    min_height: 28
    text: { label: { content: 85-334, position: center-right } }
```

Panels (`panel-light`, `panel-dark`) with the label moved to the middle right and a lower `min_height`. A panel with an entity shows the theme's accent while it's on and the dark structure tone while it's off. Leave out `text.label.content` and each block gets a random code.

### Toggle tab strip

A row of tabs whose state shows as a line along the top: dark when off, the accent when on.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-layout-card
layout:
  height: 56px
  grid-gap: 6px
  grid-template-columns: repeat(3, minmax(0, 1fr))
  grid-template-rows: minmax(0, 1fr)
cards:
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: toggle-tab
    entity: light.demo
    tap_action: { action: toggle }
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: toggle-tab
    entity: switch.demo
    tap_action: { action: toggle }
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: toggle-tab
    text: { name: { content: AUDIO } }
```

### Facing sweeps header

Two sweeps meeting across the top, with the title in the black space between them.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-layout-card
layout:
  height: 120px
  grid-gap: 6px
  grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr) minmax(0, 1fr)
  grid-template-rows: minmax(0, 1fr)
cards:
  - type: custom:lcards-elbow
    elbow:
      type: header-left
      segment:
        bar_width: 120
        bar_height: 20
        color: theme:colors.ui.primary
  - type: custom:lcards-elbow
    elbow:
      type: header-right
      segment:
        bar_width: 120
        bar_height: 20
        color: theme:colors.ui.secondary
    text:
      label:
        content: ENGINEERING
        position: center
        color: theme:colors.ui.tertiary
```

### Nested frame

The main display: a segmented frame, a thin inner bar inside a thicker outer one, opening onto black.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-elbow
grid_options: { rows: 4 }
elbow:
  type: frame
  style: segmented
  segment:
    color: theme:colors.ui.primary
  frame:
    bar_width: 30
    right:
      enabled: false
    segments:
      gap: 6
      inner_frame:
        bar_width: 10
        color: theme:colors.card.topColor
```

### Utility pills

The Picard edge column: small dark pills housed inside a bracket frame (a frame open on the outer side), with red alert at the bottom. The frame and the pills share one grid area; the pills' padding keeps them inside the frame.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-layout-card
layout:
  height: 300px
  grid-template-columns: 150px
  grid-template-rows: minmax(0, 1fr)
  grid-template-areas: |
    "col"
cards:
  - type: custom:lcards-elbow
    view_layout: { grid-area: col }
    elbow:
      type: frame
      segment: { color: theme:colors.ui.secondary }
      frame:
        bar_width: 14
        bar_height: 36
        outer_curve: 36
        left: { enabled: false }
  - type: custom:lcards-layout-card
    view_layout: { grid-area: col }
    layout:
      padding: 46px 22px 46px 4px
      grid-gap: 8px
      grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr)
      grid-template-rows: 26px 26px 26px minmax(0, 1fr) 26px
    cards:
        - { type: custom:lcards-button, preset: lozenge, min_height: 26, text: { label: { content: ZOOM, show: true, position: center, color: theme:colors.ui.secondary } }, style: { card: { color: { background: { default: theme:colors.card.topColor } } } } }
        - { type: custom:lcards-button, preset: lozenge, min_height: 26, text: { label: { content: SETTINGS, show: true, position: center, color: theme:colors.ui.secondary } }, style: { card: { color: { background: { default: theme:colors.card.topColor } } } } }
        - { type: custom:lcards-button, preset: lozenge, min_height: 26, text: { label: { content: DIMMER, show: true, position: center, color: theme:colors.ui.secondary } }, style: { card: { color: { background: { default: theme:colors.card.topColor } } } } }
        - { type: custom:lcards-button, preset: text-only, min_height: 0 }
        - type: custom:lcards-button
          preset: lozenge
          min_height: 26
          text: { label: { content: RED ALERT, show: true, position: center } }
          style:
            card:
              color:
                background:
                  default: var(--lcars-alert-color, var(--lcards-orange-dark))
          tap_action:
            action: perform-action
            perform_action: lcards.red_alert
```

### Concentric sweep

A thick sweep with a thin line running parallel inside it, the Picard header and corner shape. A segmented elbow: `outer_segment` is the sweep, `inner_segment` the line. Swap the weights for the other common Picard form: a thin outer band with a large curve (`outer_segment` about 40 by 14, `outer_curve` around 120) wrapped round a wide inner block (`inner_segment` 150 by 30), as in the lcars-shell strategy and the [split screen](dashboard-gallery#picard-split-screen).

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-elbow
grid_options: { rows: 3 }
elbow:
  type: header-left
  style: segmented
  segments:
    gap: 6
    outer_segment: { bar_width: 140, bar_height: 24, color: theme:colors.ui.secondary }
    inner_segment: { bar_width: 6, bar_height: 4, color: theme:colors.ui.primary }
text:
  title:
    content: COURSE SELECT
    position: bottom-right
    color: theme:colors.ui.tertiary
```

### Controls inside a wide arm

A thick frame whose black inset holds a group of controls, as in the Titan console side panels. The frame and a layout card share the area; the layout card's padding is a little more than the frame's bars.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-layout-card
layout:
  height: 220px
  grid-template-columns: 260px
  grid-template-rows: minmax(0, 1fr)
  grid-template-areas: |
    "arm"
cards:
  - type: custom:lcards-elbow
    view_layout: { grid-area: arm }
    elbow:
      type: frame
      segment: { color: theme:colors.ui.primary }
      frame: { bar_width: 24, bar_height: 24, outer_curve: 40, inner_curve: 18 }
  - type: custom:lcards-layout-card
    view_layout: { grid-area: arm }
    layout:
      padding: 34px
      grid-gap: 6px
      grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr
      grid-template-rows: repeat(3, 34px)
    cards:
      - { type: custom:lcards-button, preset: panel-dark, min_height: 34, text: { label: { content: 6-3390, position: center-right } } }
      - { type: custom:lcards-button, preset: panel-dark, min_height: 34, text: { label: { content: 60-1204, position: center-right } } }
      - { type: custom:lcards-button, preset: panel-dark, min_height: 34, entity: light.demo, tap_action: { action: toggle }, text: { label: { content: 5-6549, position: center-right } } }
      - { type: custom:lcards-button, preset: panel-dark, min_height: 34, text: { label: { content: 34-3719, position: center-right } } }
      - { type: custom:lcards-button, preset: panel-dark, min_height: 34, text: { label: { content: 80-1932, position: center-right } } }
      - { type: custom:lcards-button, preset: panel-dark, min_height: 34, text: { label: { content: 8-5300, position: center-right } } }
```

### Segmented bar (classic arms)

Classic screens rarely run one unbroken bar across the screen: the sweep turns into a short bar, then the bar continues as segments of different lengths and roles, each with a label. Keep the elbow's area just wider than its vertical bar, and put the segments in a row the same height as the bar.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-layout-card
layout:
  height: 110px
  grid-gap: 6px
  grid-template-columns: 220px 3fr 1fr 4fr 2fr
  grid-template-rows: 40px minmax(0, 1fr)
  grid-template-areas: |
    "corner s1 s2 s3 s4"
    "corner .  .  .  ."
cards:
  - type: custom:lcards-elbow
    view_layout: { grid-area: corner }
    elbow:
      type: header-left
      segment: { bar_width: 140, bar_height: 40, color: theme:colors.ui.primary }
  - { type: custom:lcards-button, preset: panel-light, min_height: 40, view_layout: { grid-area: s1 }, text: { label: { content: COURSE SELECT, position: bottom-right } } }
  - { type: custom:lcards-button, preset: panel-light, min_height: 40, view_layout: { grid-area: s2 }, text: { label: { content: "541", position: bottom-right } }, style: { card: { color: { background: { default: theme:colors.ui.tertiary } } } } }
  - { type: custom:lcards-button, preset: panel-light, min_height: 40, view_layout: { grid-area: s3 }, text: { label: { content: NAV REF, position: bottom-right } }, style: { card: { color: { background: { default: theme:colors.ui.secondary } } } } }
  - { type: custom:lcards-button, preset: panel-light, min_height: 40, view_layout: { grid-area: s4 }, text: { label: { content: FLIGHT, position: bottom-right } } }
```

The same works for a Picard closing bar: thin segments (14 to 20 px) in structure tones, one in the accent.

### Status rows

A label block and a long value bar per line, for readings.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-layout-card
layout:
  height: 190px
  grid-gap: 6px
  grid-template-columns: 1fr
  grid-template-rows: repeat(3, minmax(0, 1fr))
cards:
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: bar-label-left
    text: { label: { content: PRIMARY } }
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: bar-label-left
    text: { label: { content: SECONDARY } }
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: bar-label-left
    text: { label: { content: AUXILIARY } }
```

### Number cascade filler

Fills a spare area with moving numbers instead of black.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-data-grid
data_mode: decorative
grid_options: { rows: 3 }
```

### Pill grid (classic)

TNG-style: big numbers leading a group of pills, the groups in different roles.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-layout-card
layout:
  height: 180px
  grid-gap: 6px
  grid-template-columns: 70px repeat(3, minmax(0, 1fr))
  grid-template-rows: repeat(2, minmax(0, 1fr))
cards:
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: text-only
    text: { label: { content: "358", show: true, position: center-right, color: theme:colors.ui.tertiary } }
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: lozenge
    style: { card: { color: { background: { default: theme:colors.ui.primary } } } }
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: lozenge
    style: { card: { color: { background: { default: theme:colors.ui.primary } } } }
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: lozenge
    style: { card: { color: { background: { default: theme:colors.ui.secondary } } } }
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: text-only
    text: { label: { content: "451", show: true, position: center-right, color: theme:colors.ui.secondary } }
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: lozenge
    style: { card: { color: { background: { default: theme:colors.ui.secondary } } } }
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: lozenge
    style: { card: { color: { background: { default: theme:colors.ui.tertiary } } } }
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: lozenge
    style: { card: { color: { background: { default: theme:colors.ui.primary } } } }
```

To name a pill, add `text: { label: { content: WARP, show: true } }`.

### Bracket frame (classic)

DS9 and Voyager screens: a header bar with the title, a sidebar of blocks, a footer bar.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-layout-card
layout:
  height: 260px
  grid-gap: 6px
  grid-template-columns: 120px minmax(0, 1fr)
  grid-template-rows: 70px minmax(0, 1fr) minmax(0, 1fr) 70px
  grid-template-areas: |
    "top    top"
    "side1  main"
    "side2  main"
    "bottom bottom"
cards:
  - type: custom:lcards-elbow
    view_layout: { grid-area: top }
    elbow:
      type: header-left
      segment: { bar_width: 120, bar_height: 24, color: theme:colors.ui.primary }
    text:
      label:
        content: "STELLAR CARTOGRAPHY • 2387"
        position: top-right
        color: theme:colors.ui.tertiary
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: panel-dark
    view_layout: { grid-area: side1 }
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: panel-light
    view_layout: { grid-area: side2 }
  - type: custom:lcards-data-grid
    data_mode: decorative
    view_layout: { grid-area: main }
  - type: custom:lcards-elbow
    view_layout: { grid-area: bottom }
    elbow:
      type: footer-left
      segment: { bar_width: 120, bar_height: 24, color: theme:colors.ui.primary }
```

### Header bar with a title

A bar that carries the screen or section title, with a short cap before it. Picard sections (*MISSION OPS*, *PROPULSION*) use this instead of a sweep. The title grows to fill the bar's height, so in a narrow area set a smaller `text.label.font_size` (or a shorter `min_height`) or it runs off the end.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
preset: bar-label-left
min_height: 48
text:
  label:
    content: MISSION OPS
    color: theme:colors.ui.tertiary
style:
  card:
    color:
      background:
        default: theme:colors.ui.tertiary
```

### Readout rows

A label block and a horizontal gauge per line, for a set of levels read side by side.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-layout-card
layout:
  height: 190px
  grid-gap: 6px
  grid-template-columns: 130px minmax(0, 1fr)
  grid-template-rows: repeat(3, minmax(0, 1fr))
cards:
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: panel-dark
    min_height: 0
    text: { label: { content: PRIMARY, position: center-right } }
  - type: custom:lcards-slider
    entity: input_number.primary_level
    preset: gauge-basic
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: panel-dark
    min_height: 0
    text: { label: { content: SECONDARY, position: center-right } }
  - type: custom:lcards-slider
    entity: input_number.secondary_level
    preset: gauge-basic
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: panel-dark
    min_height: 0
    text: { label: { content: RESERVE, position: center-right } }
  - type: custom:lcards-slider
    entity: input_number.reserve_level
    preset: gauge-basic
```

### Gauge bank

A row of vertical gauges, as on the Picard biometric and atmospheric panels. Good for several readings of the same kind.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-layout-card
layout:
  height: 420px
  grid-gap: 10px
  grid-template-columns: repeat(4, minmax(0, 1fr))
  grid-template-rows: minmax(0, 1fr)
cards:
  - type: custom:lcards-slider
    component: picard
    preset: picard-gauge-vertical
    entity: sensor.demo_temperature
  - type: custom:lcards-slider
    component: picard
    preset: picard-gauge-vertical
    entity: sensor.demo_humidity
  - type: custom:lcards-slider
    component: picard
    preset: picard-gauge-vertical
    entity: sensor.demo_battery
  - type: custom:lcards-slider
    component: picard
    preset: picard-gauge-vertical
    entity: input_number.demo_level
```

### Selector strip

A row of equal tabs for choosing one of several, as in the Titan.DS fleet directory: a [select menu](../cards/select-menu/) with the `toggle-tab` preset, the selected option highlighted.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-select-menu
entity: input_select.demo_mode
preset: toggle-tab
grid:
  columns: 4
  gap: 6px
```

### Tile wall

Small framed tiles, each with its own reading, as in the Picard signal-processing panels. Each frame holds its reading as an embedded card ([symbiont](../cards/elbow/#symbiont)): a chart, a camera, a data grid.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-layout-card
layout:
  height: 170px
  grid-gap: 10px
  grid-template-columns: repeat(3, minmax(0, 1fr))
  grid-template-rows: minmax(0, 1fr)
cards:
  - type: custom:lcards-elbow
    elbow:
      type: frame
      segment: { color: theme:colors.card.topColor }
      frame: { bar_width: 4, bar_height: 4, outer_curve: 10 }
    symbiont:
      enabled: true
      position: { top: 10, right: 10, bottom: 10, left: 10 }
      imprint: { enabled: false }
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-data-grid
        data_mode: decorative
        format: digit
        grid:
          grid-template-rows: repeat(4, auto)
          grid-template-columns: repeat(3, minmax(0, 1fr))
  - type: custom:lcards-elbow
    elbow:
      type: frame
      segment: { color: theme:colors.card.topColor }
      frame: { bar_width: 4, bar_height: 4, outer_curve: 10 }
    symbiont:
      enabled: true
      position: { top: 10, right: 10, bottom: 10, left: 10 }
      imprint: { enabled: false }
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-data-grid
        data_mode: decorative
        format: hex
        grid:
          grid-template-rows: repeat(4, auto)
          grid-template-columns: repeat(3, minmax(0, 1fr))
  - type: custom:lcards-elbow
    elbow:
      type: frame
      segment: { color: theme:colors.ui.tertiary }
      frame: { bar_width: 4, bar_height: 4, outer_curve: 10 }
    symbiont:
      enabled: true
      position: { top: 10, right: 10, bottom: 10, left: 10 }
      imprint: { enabled: false }
      card:
        type: custom:lcards-data-grid
        data_mode: decorative
        format: float
        grid:
          grid-template-rows: repeat(4, auto)
          grid-template-columns: repeat(3, minmax(0, 1fr))
```

### Split header (classic)

The TNG and Voyager header: an upper block that sweeps down into a bar, a thin gap, and a lower block that sweeps out of the next bar. The title sits in the black beside the upper sweep.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-layout-card
layout:
  height: 200px
  grid-gap: 8px
  grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr)
  grid-template-rows: minmax(0, 1fr) minmax(0, 1fr)
cards:
  - type: custom:lcards-elbow
    elbow:
      type: footer-left
      segment: { bar_width: 140, bar_height: 18, color: theme:colors.ui.primary }
    text:
      title:
        content: PATIENT BIOMEDICAL STATUS
        position: top-right
        font_size: 26
        color: theme:colors.ui.tertiary
  - type: custom:lcards-elbow
    elbow:
      type: header-left
      segment: { bar_width: 140, bar_height: 18, color: theme:colors.ui.secondary }
```

### List

Rows of text in columns, for rosters, schedules and logs, as in Voyager's duty roster. A [data grid](../cards/data-grid/) in data mode with fixed text or your entities.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-data-grid
data_mode: data
rows:
  - values: [Name, Station, Shift]
    header: true
  - [TUVOK, SECURITY, ALPHA]
  - [TORRES, ENGINEERING, BETA]
  - [PARIS, CONN, ALPHA]
  - [KIM, OPS, GAMMA]
grid:
  grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr 90px
  gap: 4px
style:
  font_size: 20px
columns:
  - style:
      align: left
      color: theme:colors.ui.tertiary
```

### Slanted bars

Bars with a cut end, for labels and indicators (Titan console side panels). The elbow's `bar-slant-right`, `bar-slant-left` and `bar-parallelogram` types make the whole card one bar; `segment.diagonal_angle` sets the cut.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-layout-card
layout:
  height: 96px
  grid-gap: 8px
  grid-template-columns: 200px 120px
  grid-template-rows: 44px 44px
cards:
  - type: custom:lcards-elbow
    elbow: { type: bar-slant-right, segment: { color: theme:colors.ui.secondary } }
    text: { label: { content: LCARS, position: center-left, font_size: 22, color: "var(--lcars-text-dark, black)" } }
  - type: custom:lcards-elbow
    elbow: { type: bar-parallelogram, segment: { color: theme:colors.ui.tertiary, diagonal_angle: 60 } }
  - type: custom:lcards-elbow
    elbow: { type: bar-slant-right, segment: { color: theme:colors.ui.primary } }
    text: { label: { content: "47", position: center-left, font_size: 22, color: "var(--lcars-text-dark, black)" } }
```

### Flagged blocks

Number blocks with a thin accent tick on the left, as in the Titan console's number columns: the `panel-flagged` preset.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-layout-card
layout:
  height: 150px
  grid-gap: 6px
  grid-template-columns: 140px
  grid-template-rows: repeat(4, minmax(0, 1fr))
cards:
  - { type: custom:lcards-button, preset: panel-flagged, min_height: 0, text: { label: { content: "012" } } }
  - { type: custom:lcards-button, preset: panel-flagged, min_height: 0, text: { label: { content: "330" } } }
  - { type: custom:lcards-button, preset: panel-flagged, min_height: 0, entity: light.demo, tap_action: { action: toggle }, text: { label: { content: "436" } } }
  - { type: custom:lcards-button, preset: panel-flagged, min_height: 0, text: { label: { content: "542" } } }
```

### Dot rows

Rows of dots in groups, along the top or bottom edge of a frame (Titan.DS headers and footers). A text-only button with runs of `•`.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
preset: text-only
min_height: 24
text:
  label:
    content: "•  •••  ••  •••••  •  ••  •••"
    show: true
    position: center-right
    color: theme:colors.ui.secondary
```

### Fleet tiles

A row of framed tiles, one per item, as in the Titan.DS fleet directory: a frame elbow per tile with its name and class; the thicker bottom bar can carry a state colour.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-layout-card
layout:
  height: 150px
  grid-gap: 8px
  grid-template-columns: repeat(3, minmax(0, 1fr))
  grid-template-rows: minmax(0, 1fr)
cards:
  - type: custom:lcards-elbow
    elbow: { type: frame, segment: { color: theme:colors.card.topColor }, frame: { bar_width: 4, bar_height: 18, outer_curve: 8 } }
    text:
      label: { content: NCC-1701-A, position: top-center, font_size: 14, color: theme:colors.ui.tertiary }
      class: { content: CONSTITUTION, position: center, font_size: 18, color: theme:colors.ui.primary }
  - type: custom:lcards-elbow
    elbow: { type: frame, segment: { color: theme:colors.ui.secondary }, frame: { bar_width: 4, bar_height: 18, outer_curve: 8 } }
    text:
      label: { content: NCC-1701-C, position: top-center, font_size: 14, color: theme:colors.ui.tertiary }
      class: { content: AMBASSADOR, position: center, font_size: 18, color: theme:colors.ui.primary }
  - type: custom:lcards-elbow
    elbow: { type: frame, segment: { color: theme:colors.card.topColor }, frame: { bar_width: 4, bar_height: 18, outer_curve: 8 } }
    text:
      label: { content: NCC-1701-E, position: top-center, font_size: 14, color: theme:colors.ui.tertiary }
      class: { content: SOVEREIGN, position: center, font_size: 18, color: theme:colors.ui.primary }
```

### Brackets and scopes

Round displays framed by bracket arcs, and radar scopes (meWho's Titan.DS and Protostar screens): the button's `brackets` and `radar` [components](../cards/button/#component-mode-brackets-and-radar). Both take their colours from the theme roles.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-layout-card
layout:
  height: 300px
  grid-gap: 12px
  grid-template-columns: 300px 300px
  grid-template-rows: minmax(0, 1fr)
cards:
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    component: brackets
    text: { label: { content: "88", show: true, position: center, font_size: 48, color: theme:colors.ui.tertiary } }
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    component: radar
```

## Putting it together

A screen is a [layout view](../cards/layout-view/) shaped by one of the [archetypes](#screen-archetypes), with patterns in its areas: for example a facing-sweeps header across the top, a code-block column and utility pills down the left, a nested frame with an MSD or chart in the centre, a toggle tab strip along the bottom. Or a portrait panel: a header bar with a title, a gauge bank, a selector strip. The [Dashboard Gallery](dashboard-gallery#built-from-the-design-guide) has six complete screens built this way, three per look, each from a different archetype.

---

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/getting-started/what-is-lcards.html -->

# What is LCARdS?

![LCARdS Banner](/img/lcards-banner.gif)

**Build Star Trek LCARS-style dashboards in Home Assistant.**

LCARdS is a set of LCARS cards (buttons, elbows, sliders, charts, data grids, ship displays and more) that work together as one system. It is designed to pair with the [HA-LCARS theme](https://github.com/th3jesta/ha-lcars).

## How it works

Three layers, plus a small integration running inside Home Assistant.

## What that gives you

- **Colours that follow state:** a button lights up when its light is on, a reading turns red past a threshold. No automations needed.
- **One look everywhere:** every card takes its colours, fonts and sizes from the same theme, so the whole screen matches.
- **Screen-wide reactions:** [rules](../core/rules/) restyle many cards at once, and [alert mode](../core/alert-mode) repaints the whole dashboard.
- **Live values anywhere:** put a sensor value, a smoothed reading or a [template](../core/templates/) in any label.
- **Motion and sound:** [animations](../core/animations) and LCARS [sounds](../core/sounds) on taps and state changes.
- **Control from automations:** [actions](../configuration/ha-actions) like `lcards.red_alert` work from scripts, automations and voice.

## Next steps

1. **[Install LCARdS](installation)**: through HACS, in a few minutes.
2. **[Build a dashboard](building-dashboards)**: pick cards and lay out a screen.
3. **[Browse the gallery](dashboard-gallery)**: copy a complete dashboard and make it yours.
4. **[Get AI help](ai-assistance)**: let an assistant write the YAML for you.

::: info A hobby project
LCARdS is a fan-made hobby project, not a fully commissioned Starfleet product: expect the occasional tribble. If something in these docs doesn't match what you see, please [open an issue](https://github.com/snootched/lcards/issues).
:::

---

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/configuration/ -->

# Configuration

LCARdS configuration is managed through the **LCARdS Config Panel**, a dedicated sidebar entry in Home Assistant that serves as the central control hub for your installation. It provides access to helper management, theme browsing, alert mode customisation, sound configuration, content pack exploration, and device/user management.

The panel is registered automatically when the LCARdS integration is installed.

::: tip New install?
Start with [First setup](../getting-started/installation#_3-first-setup): create the helpers, then tune alert modes and sounds.
:::

---

## Accessing the Panel

Look for the **LCARdS Config** entry in the Home Assistant sidebar after installation. If it is not visible:

1. Go to **Settings → Integrations → LCARdS → Configure**
2. Enable **Show sidebar panel**
3. The panel appears immediately: no restart needed

You can also customise the sidebar title and icon from the same screen.

---

## Panel Tabs

### Welcome

The first tab when opening the Config Panel:

- **Get Started checklist**: step-by-step onboarding: create helpers, configure alert mode, set up sounds
- **Panel Guide**: clickable cards for each tab with a short description; clicking navigates directly to that tab
- **Resource links**: documentation, GitHub, and community links

---

### Helpers

::: tip First launch
Open the **Helpers** tab and click **Create All Helpers** before using anything else. This creates any missing HA input helper LCARdS uses for alert mode, sounds, and sizing in one step.  HA-LCARS theme helpers can also be created here.
:::

Shows all LCARdS HA input helpers, their current values, and creation status:

- Create all required helpers in one click (**Create All Helpers**)
- Inspect or manually set individual helper values
- Identify missing helpers that may affect card behaviour

Helpers are standard Home Assistant `input_*` entities and persist across restarts.

→ [Persistent Helpers reference](persistent-helpers.md)

---

### Theme Studio

The theme tools, one per tab:

- **LCARdS Alert Mode Lab**: customise the colour palette applied per alert level (`red_alert`, `yellow_alert`, `blue_alert`, `gray_alert`, `black_alert`). Adjust hue, saturation, lightness, and anchor parameters, preview changes live across your dashboard, then save to helpers.
- **HA-LCARS Theme Lab**: build your own HA-LCARS theme profile, with full palettes, LCARS chrome and state colours. See [HA-LCARS Theme Lab](ha-lcars-theme-lab).
- **LCARdS Theme Tokens**, **LCARS CSS Variables**, **All CSS Variables**: browse the active theme's tokens and the page's CSS variables. Find the exact `theme:colors.ui.primary` path to use in card config, or which CSS variable controls a colour.
- **Token Overrides**: change a token's value globally, per user or per device.

A card editor's **Main Engineering > Theme** tab lists the tokens that card uses and links here. The link `/lcards-config?tab=theme` opens this tab directly (other tabs: `helpers`, `connectivity`, `sounds`, `users`, `packs`, `storage`).

→ [Alert Mode Lab](alert-mode-lab.md) &nbsp;·&nbsp; [Alert Mode](../core/alert-mode.md) &nbsp;·&nbsp; [Themes](../core/themes/)

---

### Connectivity

Configure a full-screen overlay displayed when connection to Home Assistant is lost, ideal for kiosk installs where you always want to know when the dashboard is offline.

- **Enable / disable** the overlay globally, per user, or per device
- **Simple text**: configure stylized messages
- **Custom card**: replace the simple text message with any HA card(s)
- **Connection Restored**: optional auto-dismissing confirmation shown on reconnect
- **Effect layers**: independently configure the canvas animation, colour overlay, and backdrop filter applied behind the message

→ [Connectivity](connectivity.md)

---

### Sounds

Configure LCARS-style audio feedback for card interactions and alert events:

- Enable or disable sound categories (card interactions, UI navigation, alert sounds)
- Select the active sound scheme
- Set per-event overrides: change or mute individual sound events
- Control master volume
- **Per-user / per-device overrides**: set different sound preferences for your own browser session without changing global defaults

→ [Sounds](./sounds.md)

---

### Users & Devices

Manage devices and users that have stored per-device or per-user setting overrides (introduced in LCARdS v2026.3.0)

- **Current Session** (all users): view your device identity, set a display name for this browser
- **Users** (admin only): list users with stored overrides; clear overrides for a user
- **Devices** (admin only): list registered devices with last-seen times; rename or delete device records

→ [Users & Devices](users-devices.md)

---

### Pack Explorer

Browse all installed LCARdS content packs. For each pack you can inspect:

- **Style presets**: button and slider preset definitions
- **Animations**: available animation presets and their parameters
- **Themes**: theme tokens contributed by the pack
- **Sound schemes**: audio asset sets registered by the pack

Built-in packs (core, buttons, sliders, effects, themes) are always shown. User-installed packs appear here once loaded.

---

### Storage [advanced]

:::warning **Advanced: use with caution.**
This tab exposes the raw key/value store on the backend integration.  LCARdS uses this for persistent configuration settings that are not controlled with helpers.
:::

- **Live key list**: all keys currently stored
- **Expandable JSON viewer**: inspect the value of any key
- **Inline JSON editor**: edit a value directly
- **Per-key delete**: remove a single key with confirmation
- **Reset All**: wipe the entire LCARdS store (requires explicit confirmation)

Typical use cases: debugging unexpected behaviour, recovering from a corrupt config value, or inspecting stored scoped settings.

---

---

## HA-LCARS Theme Profiles

[HA-LCARS](https://github.com/th3jesta/ha-lcars) includes two LCARdS theme profiles. They map the LCARdS colour palette to both the HA-LCARS chrome variables and the core HA colour token scale, so stock HA components, LCARdS cards, and the HA-LCARS chrome all share the same palette, including alert-mode hue rotations. Pick one as your Home Assistant theme; there is nothing to install separately.

→ [HA-LCARS Theme Profiles](ha-lcars-theme-profiles.md)

---

- [Installation](../getting-started/installation.md): how the panel is registered via the integration
- [Persistent Helpers](persistent-helpers.md): full helper reference and manual YAML setup
- [Alert Mode Lab](alert-mode-lab.md): colour palette customisation
- [Alert Mode](../core/alert-mode.md): how alert mode works and how to trigger it
