<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/chart/playground.html -->

# Chart Playground

Edit the YAML and the chart redraws as you type. Pick a starting point from the list, or paste a chart from your own dashboard.

**You don't need to know the YAML to start:**

- **Quick settings** above the editor change the most common options for you.
- **Type in the editor** and it suggests the options that fit where your cursor is, with a short description. Press **Ctrl+Space** to see suggestions anywhere, and hover over a key to read what it does.
- **Options here** (under the editor) lists everything you can add at the cursor. **Insert** adds it at the right indent, and **Docs** opens its section in a new tab.

<ClientOnly>

</ClientOnly>

## How the preview works

The preview uses the chart card's own code: the same option handling, grouping, time window, theme colours and validation as on your dashboard. The docs site has no Home Assistant, so:

- **Entities get generated sample data.** Names containing `temperature`, `humidity`, `power`, `energy` or `battery` get a realistic signal, and `light.*`/`switch.*`/`binary_sensor.*` entities switch on and off. Any other entity gets a generic wave.
- **Long-term statistics** are computed from the same sample signal.
- **Data source series** plot their entity's sample signal. Processors (smoothing, rates, ...) only run on a real dashboard.
- **`theme:` tokens** resolve on a real dashboard; the preview shows their fallback colours.

Messages under the chart show schema warnings, and explain how an [older format](./upgrading) would be converted.

When it looks right, **Copy YAML** and paste it into your card's YAML editor, then swap in your own entities.

---

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/chart/series.html -->

# Series & Time

What each series plots, how much time the chart shows, and how to combine points, mix chart types and add Y axes. For where series data comes from (entity history, long-term statistics or an LCARdS data source), see the [Overview](./#where-the-data-comes-from).

---

## Series options

These work on every kind of series.

| Option | What it does |
|--------|--------------|
| `name` | Name in the legend and tooltip (default: the entity's friendly name) |
| `unit` | Unit in tooltips and axis labels (default: the entity's unit) |
| `float_precision` | Decimal places in tooltips |
| `color` | Series colour: any colour, `var(--lcars-...)` or theme token |
| `type` | Draw this series differently from the chart: `line`, `area`, `column` or `scatter` |
| `curve` | `smooth` (default), `straight`, `stepline` or `monotoneCubic` |
| `stroke_width` | Line width |
| `stroke_dash` | Dash length; `0` is a solid line |
| `opacity` | Fill opacity for areas and columns (0 to 1) |
| `yaxis_id` | Put the series on another Y axis: see [Y axes](#y-axes) |
| `group_by` | Combine points into time buckets: see [Grouping](#grouping) |

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
sources:
  - entity: sensor.house_power
    name: Power
    color: var(--lcars-orange)
    stroke_width: 3
  - entity: sensor.solar_power
    name: Solar
    type: area
    opacity: 0.3
    curve: straight
```

### Line styles

`curve`, `stroke_width` and `stroke_dash` per series:

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
graph_span: 12h
sources:
  - entity: sensor.kitchen_temperature
    name: smooth
    curve: smooth
  - entity: sensor.bedroom_temperature
    name: straight, dashed
    curve: straight
    stroke_dash: 6
  - entity: sensor.office_temperature
    name: stepline, thick
    curve: stepline
    stroke_width: 4
style:
  legend:
    show: true
```

### Units and decimals

`unit` and `float_precision` set what the tooltip shows (hover the chart). Without them, the entity's own unit is used:

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
sources:
  - entity: sensor.house_power
    name: Power
    unit: watts
    float_precision: 0
  - entity: sensor.outdoor_temperature
    name: Outside
    float_precision: 2
    yaxis_id: temperature
yaxis:
  - id: power
  - id: temperature
    opposite: true
```

---

## Time window

`graph_span` sets how much time the chart shows. It defaults to `24h`, and the window always ends now, moving along as time passes.

```yaml
graph_span: 6h     # also: 30min, 2d, 1w, 1mo, 1y
```

Use `span` to line the window up with the calendar, or to look back in time. This chart shows all of yesterday:

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
graph_span: 24h
span:
  start: day        # start at midnight today
  offset: -1d       # then move the window back one day
sources:
  - entity: sensor.outdoor_temperature
```

Today so far (the window runs to midnight, so the line stops at "now"):

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
graph_span: 24h
span:
  start: day
sources:
  - entity: sensor.outdoor_temperature
    name: Today
```

The last hour, in detail:

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
graph_span: 1h
sources:
  - entity: sensor.house_power
    name: Power
    curve: straight
```

This week so far, Monday to Sunday, from daily statistics:

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
chart_type: column
graph_span: 7d
span:
  start: week
sources:
  - entity: sensor.outdoor_temperature
    name: Daily high
    statistics:
      type: max
      period: day
```

| `span` option | What it does |
|---------------|--------------|
| `start` | The window starts at the beginning of the current `minute`, `hour`, `day`, `week`, `month` or `year` and lasts `graph_span` |
| `end` | The window ends at the end of the current unit (and starts `graph_span` earlier) |
| `offset` | Moves the window, e.g. `-1d` (a day earlier) or `+2h` |

---

## Grouping

`group_by` combines the points in each time bucket into one value. Use it to smooth out busy sensors, to show hourly averages over a week, or to turn readings into daily totals.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
chart_type: column
graph_span: 24h
sources:
  - entity: sensor.house_power
    name: Peak power per hour
    group_by:
      func: max        # how each bucket is combined
      duration: 1h     # bucket length
      fill: last       # buckets with no readings: last | null (leave a gap) | zero
```

| `func` | Each bucket shows |
|--------|-------------------|
| `avg` | The average |
| `min`, `max`, `median` | The lowest, highest or middle value |
| `sum` | The total |
| `first`, `last` | The first or last reading |
| `delta` | How much the value changed within the bucket |
| `diff` | How much the value changed since the previous bucket (useful for meters) |
| `minmax` | The low and high value, for [range areas](#range-charts) |
| `box` | Min, quartiles, median and max, for [box plots](#range-charts) |
| `ohlc` | Open, high, low and close, for [candlesticks](#range-charts) |

Smoothing a noisy sensor: the raw readings, and the same sensor averaged over 30 minutes:

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
graph_span: 12h
sources:
  - entity: sensor.house_power
    name: Raw
    stroke_width: 1
    color: var(--lcars-gray)
  - entity: sensor.house_power
    name: 30 min average
    stroke_width: 3
    group_by:
      func: avg
      duration: 30min
style:
  legend:
    show: true
```

Energy per hour from a meter that only counts up, using `delta`:

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
chart_type: column
graph_span: 24h
sources:
  - entity: sensor.energy_consumption
    name: kWh per hour
    group_by:
      func: delta
      duration: 1h
```

::: tip Grouping or statistics?
For long spans of a sensor with a `state_class`, [long-term statistics](./#where-the-data-comes-from) are usually better: Home Assistant has already done the summarising. Grouping works on any series, including entity history and data sources.
:::

---

## Long-term statistics

The `type` picks which of Home Assistant's summaries to plot. Three series of the same sensor show each day's low, average and high over two weeks:

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
graph_span: 14d
sources:
  - entity: sensor.outdoor_temperature
    name: Low
    color: var(--lcars-blue)
    statistics: { type: min, period: day }
    stroke_dash: 4
  - entity: sensor.outdoor_temperature
    name: Average
    color: var(--lcars-orange)
    statistics: { type: mean, period: day }
    stroke_width: 3
  - entity: sensor.outdoor_temperature
    name: High
    color: var(--lcars-red)
    statistics: { type: max, period: day }
    stroke_dash: 4
style:
  legend:
    show: true
```

| `type` | Each period shows | Typical sensors |
|--------|-------------------|-----------------|
| `mean`, `min`, `max` | The average, lowest or highest value | Temperature, humidity, power (`state_class: measurement`) |
| `change` | How much a meter increased | Energy, water, gas (`total` / `total_increasing`) |
| `sum`, `state` | The meter's running total, or its reading at the end of the period | Same |

---

## Range charts

Range charts need several values per point: a low and a high, or open/high/low/close. `group_by` builds them from any series.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
chart_type: candlestick
graph_span: 2d
sources:
  - entity: sensor.outdoor_temperature
    name: Outside
    group_by:
      func: ohlc
      duration: 3h
```

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
chart_type: boxPlot
graph_span: 7d
sources:
  - entity: sensor.house_power
    name: Power spread per day
    group_by:
      func: box
      duration: 1d
```

A range band straight from statistics, no grouping needed:

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
chart_type: rangeArea
graph_span: 14d
sources:
  - entity: sensor.outdoor_temperature
    name: Daily range
    statistics:
      type: mean
      period: day
```

| Chart type | Set the series' `group_by.func` to |
|------------|-----------------------------------|
| `rangeArea` | `minmax`. Or use long-term statistics: the band runs from each period's minimum to maximum |
| `boxPlot` | `box` |
| `candlestick` | `ohlc` |

---

## Mixing chart types

A series' `type` overrides the chart type, so one chart can show columns and lines together:

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
chart_type: line
sources:
  - entity: sensor.energy_consumption
    name: Energy per hour
    type: column
    unit: kWh
    group_by:
      func: delta
      duration: 1h
  - entity: sensor.outdoor_temperature
    name: Outside
    yaxis_id: temperature
    group_by:
      func: avg
      duration: 1h
yaxis:
  - id: energy
  - id: temperature
    opposite: true
```

::: tip Columns next to lines
In a mixed chart, columns are sized by the closest pair of points in *any* series. If the line has a reading every few minutes, the columns become thin lines. Group the line to the same bucket length as the columns (here `1h`), as above.
:::

---

## Y axes

All series share one Y axis that scales automatically. When series have very different ranges (temperature and humidity, say), give them their own axes:

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
yaxis:
  - id: temperature
  - id: humidity
    opposite: true      # draw it on the right
    min: 0
    max: 100
    decimals: 0
sources:
  - entity: sensor.living_room_temperature
    name: Temperature
  - entity: sensor.living_room_humidity
    name: Humidity
    yaxis_id: humidity
```

Series without a `yaxis_id` use the first axis. Axis labels show the series' unit.

A fixed range keeps the scale steady as values change, here a humidity axis pinned to 0 to 100:

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
chart_type: area
yaxis:
  - id: humidity
    min: 0
    max: 100
    decimals: 0
sources:
  - entity: sensor.living_room_humidity
    name: Humidity
    opacity: 0.3
```

| Axis option | What it does |
|-------------|--------------|
| `id` | Name the series refer to with `yaxis_id` (required) |
| `show` | Show the axis (default `true`) |
| `opposite` | Draw it on the right |
| `min`, `max` | Fixed range; leave them out to scale automatically |
| `decimals` | Decimal places in the labels |

---

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/chart/styling.html -->

# Styling

Charts use your theme's colours and fonts without any `style` at all, so everything on this page is optional. Colours accept every format in [Colours](../../core/colours.md): `var(--lcars-*)`, `theme:` tokens, hex and rgba.

For per-series colours and line styles, the [series options](./series#series-options) (`color`, `stroke_width`, `curve`, ...) are usually simpler than the lists below.

---

## Reference lines

Horizontal lines at fixed values:

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
sources:
  - entity: sensor.outdoor_temperature
    name: Outside
style:
  zero_line: true
  thresholds:
    - value: 18
      label: Warm
      color: var(--lcars-red)
    - value: 8
      label: Cold
      color: var(--lcars-blue)
      dash: true
```

| Option | What it does |
|--------|--------------|
| `style.zero_line` | Draw a line at 0 |
| `style.zero_line_color` | Its colour |
| `style.thresholds` | A list of lines, each with the options below |

| Threshold option | What it does |
|------------------|--------------|
| `value` | Where the line goes (required) |
| `label` | Text on the line |
| `color` | Line colour |
| `width` | Line width (default 2) |
| `dash` | Dashed line |
| `opacity` | Line opacity (default 0.7) |

---

## Colours

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `style.colors.series` | list | Series colours, used in order |
| `style.colors.stroke` | list | Line/outline colours |
| `style.colors.fill` | list | Area fill colours |
| `style.colors.background` | string | Chart background |
| `style.colors.foreground` | string | Default text and label colour |
| `style.colors.grid` | string | Grid line colour |
| `style.colors.marker.fill` | list | Point fill colours (default: the series colours) |
| `style.colors.marker.stroke` | list | Point outline colours |
| `style.colors.axis.x` | string | X-axis label colour |
| `style.colors.axis.y` | string | Y-axis label colour |
| `style.colors.axis.border` | string | Axis line colour |
| `style.colors.axis.ticks` | string | Tick mark colour |
| `style.colors.legend.default` | string | Legend text colour |
| `style.colors.legend.items` | list | Per-series legend colours |
| `style.colors.data_labels` | list | Value label colours |

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
chart_type: area
sources:
  - entity: sensor.kitchen_temperature
    name: Kitchen
  - entity: sensor.bedroom_temperature
    name: Bedroom
style:
  colors:
    series:
      - "var(--lcars-yellow)"
      - "var(--lcars-violet)"
    grid: "var(--lcars-gray)"
  fill:
    type: gradient
    gradient:
      opacityFrom: 0.5
      opacityTo: 0.05
  legend:
    show: true
```

---

## Lines and fills

### `style.stroke`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| `style.stroke.width` | number | `2` | Line width in px |
| `style.stroke.curve` | string | `smooth` | `smooth`, `straight`, `stepline`, `monotoneCubic` |
| `style.stroke.dash_array` | number | `0` | Dash length; `0` is solid |

### `style.fill`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| `style.fill.type` | string | `solid` | `solid`, `gradient`, `pattern`, `image` |
| `style.fill.opacity` | number | `0.7` | Fill opacity |
| `style.fill.gradient.shade` | string | - | `light` or `dark` |
| `style.fill.gradient.type` | string | - | `horizontal`, `vertical`, `diagonal1`, `diagonal2` |
| `style.fill.gradient.shadeIntensity` | number | - | Shade intensity |
| `style.fill.gradient.opacityFrom` | number | - | Opacity where the gradient starts |
| `style.fill.gradient.opacityTo` | number | - | Opacity where the gradient ends |

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
graph_span: 12h
sources:
  - entity: sensor.outdoor_temperature
    name: Outside
style:
  stroke:
    width: 3
    dash_array: 8
    curve: straight
```

### `style.markers`

Points drawn on each value.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| `style.markers.size` | number | `0` | Point size in px; `0` hides them |
| `style.markers.shape` | string | `circle` | `circle`, `square`, `rect`, `diamond`, `triangle`, `star`, `cross`, `plus` |
| `style.markers.stroke.width` | number | `2` | Point outline width in px |

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
graph_span: 12h
sources:
  - entity: sensor.outdoor_temperature
    name: Outside
    group_by:
      func: avg
      duration: 1h
style:
  markers:
    size: 6
    shape: diamond
    stroke:
      width: 1
```

---

## Grid, legend and labels

### `style.grid`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| `style.grid.show` | boolean | `true` | Show grid lines |
| `style.grid.stroke_dash_array` | number | `4` | Grid line dash length |
| `style.grid.row_colors` | list | - | Alternating row background colours |
| `style.grid.column_colors` | list | - | Alternating column background colours |

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
chart_type: column
sources:
  - entity: sensor.house_power
    name: Power
    group_by:
      func: avg
      duration: 2h
style:
  grid:
    stroke_dash_array: 0
    row_colors:
      - "rgba(255, 153, 0, 0.08)"
      - "transparent"
```

### `style.legend`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| `style.legend.show` | boolean | `false` (`true` for `pie`, `donut`, `polarArea` and `radialBar`) | Show the legend. The slice and gauge charts turn it on because it names the series |
| `style.legend.position` | string | `bottom` | `top`, `bottom`, `left`, `right` |
| `style.legend.horizontalAlign` | string | `center` | `left`, `center`, `right` |
| `style.legend.font_size` | number | font size + 2 | Legend font size in px |

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
sources:
  - entity: sensor.kitchen_temperature
    name: Kitchen
  - entity: sensor.bedroom_temperature
    name: Bedroom
  - entity: sensor.office_temperature
    name: Office
style:
  legend:
    show: true
    position: right
    font_size: 13
```

### `style.data_labels`

Values written on the chart.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| `style.data_labels.show` | boolean | `false` | Show value labels |
| `style.data_labels.offsetY` | number | `0` | Vertical offset in px |
| `style.data_labels.font_size` | number | font size | Label font size in px |

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
chart_type: column
graph_span: 7d
sources:
  - entity: sensor.outdoor_temperature
    name: Daily high
    statistics:
      type: max
      period: day
style:
  data_labels:
    show: true
    font_size: 11
  yaxis:
    decimals: 0
```

### `style.xaxis` and `style.yaxis`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| `style.xaxis.labels.show` | boolean | `true` | Show X-axis labels |
| `style.xaxis.labels.rotate` | number | `0` | Label rotation in degrees (category axes only; time axes don't rotate) |
| `style.xaxis.border.show` | boolean | `false` | Show the X-axis line |
| `style.xaxis.ticks.show` | boolean | `false` | Show X-axis tick marks |
| `style.yaxis.labels.show` | boolean | `true` | Show Y-axis labels |
| `style.yaxis.decimals` | number | - | Decimal places for labels, tooltips and value labels |
| `style.yaxis.border.show` | boolean | `false` | Show the Y-axis line |
| `style.yaxis.ticks.show` | boolean | `false` | Show Y-axis tick marks |

The X axis shows time by default. Set `xaxis_type: category` or `xaxis_type: numeric` at the top level for other kinds of X values. For several Y axes, use [`yaxis`](./series#y-axes).

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
graph_span: 48h
sources:
  - entity: sensor.outdoor_temperature
    name: Outside
style:
  xaxis:
    border:
      show: true
    ticks:
      show: true
  yaxis:
    decimals: 1
    border:
      show: true
```

### `style.display`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| `style.display.toolbar` | boolean | `false` | Show the zoom/download toolbar |
| `style.display.tooltip.show` | boolean | `true` | Show the hover tooltip |
| `style.display.tooltip.theme` | string | `dark` | `dark` or `light` |

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
graph_span: 6h
sources:
  - entity: sensor.house_power
    name: Power
style:
  display:
    toolbar: true
    tooltip:
      theme: light
```

### `style.typography`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| `style.typography.font_family` | string | your theme's font | Font for all chart text |
| `style.typography.font_size` | number | `12` | Base font size in px |

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
sources:
  - entity: sensor.outdoor_temperature
    name: Outside
style:
  typography:
    font_size: 16
```

### `style.theme`

ApexCharts' own palette options. Explicit colours take priority.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| `style.theme.mode` | string | `dark` | `dark` or `light` |
| `style.theme.palette` | string | - | ApexCharts palette (`palette1` to `palette10`) |
| `style.theme.monochrome.enabled` | boolean | `false` | Shades of a single colour |
| `style.theme.monochrome.color` | string | - | The base colour |
| `style.theme.monochrome.shade_to` | string | `dark` | `dark` or `light` |
| `style.theme.monochrome.shade_intensity` | number | `0.65` | How far the shades spread |

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
chart_type: donut
sources:
  - entity: sensor.kitchen_power
    name: Kitchen
  - entity: sensor.office_power
    name: Office
  - entity: sensor.garage_power
    name: Garage
  - entity: sensor.laundry_power
    name: Laundry
style:
  theme:
    monochrome:
      enabled: true
      color: "#ff9900"
      shade_to: dark
  legend:
    show: true
```

---

## Chart-type options

| Field | Chart type | Default | Description |
|-------|------------|---------|-------------|
| `style.gauge_start_angle` | `radialBar` | `-90` | Where the gauge arc starts, in degrees |
| `style.gauge_end_angle` | `radialBar` | `90` | Where it ends |
| `style.gauge_total` | `radialBar` | `false` | Show the sum of all gauges in the centre |
| `style.value_format` | `radialBar` | - | `percent` adds a % sign to the values |
| `style.group_rows` | `rangeBar` | `true` | Put bars with the same label on one row |
| `style.show_labels` | `rangeBar` | `true` | Show labels on the bars |

### Fitted by default

Some chart types are laid out by the card rather than left to ApexCharts' defaults, which waste space in wide cards. These follow the card when it changes size; [raw options](#raw-apexcharts-options) still override them.

| Chart type | Default |
|------------|---------|
| `radar` | The web is sized to fill the card (with room for the axis names) and centred, so a three-axis triangle doesn't leave the bottom empty. No line-chart grid behind it. Set `plotOptions.radar.size` (radius in px) and `offsetY` in `chart_options` to place it yourself |
| `radialBar` | A half-circle gauge (start and end angles within -90 to 90) fills the card's height instead of reserving room for the missing lower half |
| `polarArea` | The ring values are hidden (they sit on the vertical spoke). `style.yaxis.labels.show: true` brings them back |
| `candlestick` | One series: green candles for up, red for down. Two or more: each series' candles take its own colour (full for up, darker for down), so they match the legend and stay apart. Set `plotOptions.candlestick.colors.upward` and `downward` in `chart_options` to choose |
| `bar` | Horizontal bars over time label each bar with its time on the vertical axis and put the values along the bottom |

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
chart_type: radialBar
sources:
  - entity: sensor.phone_battery
    name: Phone
  - entity: sensor.tablet_battery
    name: Tablet
style:
  gauge_start_angle: -135
  gauge_end_angle: 135
  value_format: percent
  legend:
    show: true
```

---

## Formatters

Format strings for axis labels and tooltips. These use a small chart-only syntax; they are **not** LCARdS templates.

| Field | Examples |
|-------|----------|
| `style.formatters.xaxis_label` | `HH:mm` · `MMM DD` · `ddd HH:mm` |
| `style.formatters.yaxis_label` | `{value}°C` · `{value}%` |
| `style.formatters.tooltip` | `{seriesName}: {y}` · `{x\|MMM DD HH:mm}: {y}°C` |

- **Dates:** `YYYY`, `YY`, `MMMM` (October), `MMM` (Oct), `MM`, `M`, `dddd` (Tuesday), `ddd` (Tue), `DD`, `D`, `HH`, `H`, `hh`, `h`, `mm`, `m`, `ss`, `s`, `A` (PM), `a` (pm). Put literal text in square brackets: `[at] HH:mm`.
- **Values:** `{value}` in axis labels; `{y}`, `{x}`, `{x|format}` and `{seriesName}` in tooltips.

Units and decimal places usually need no formatter: set `unit` and `float_precision` on the series.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
sources:
  - entity: sensor.outdoor_temperature
    name: Outside
style:
  formatters:
    xaxis_label: "ddd HH:mm"
    yaxis_label: "{value}°"
    tooltip: "{x|ddd [at] HH:mm}: {y}°C"
```

---

## Animation

```yaml
style:
  animation:
    preset: lcars_standard
```

The chart below uses `lcars_dramatic`; reload the page to see it again.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
chart_type: column
sources:
  - entity: sensor.house_power
    name: Power
    group_by:
      func: avg
      duration: 1h
style:
  animation:
    preset: lcars_dramatic
```

| Preset | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `lcars_standard` | Smooth entrance (the default feel) |
| `lcars_dramatic` | Slower, more theatrical entrance |
| `lcars_minimal` | Quick, subtle entrance |
| `lcars_realtime` | No entrance animation; quick updates for live data |
| `lcars_alert` | Fast entrance for alert displays |
| `none` | No animation |

---

## Raw ApexCharts options

`style.chart_options` passes options straight to ApexCharts and overrides everything above. Use it only for things LCARdS doesn't cover: see the [ApexCharts options reference](https://apexcharts.com/docs/options/).

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
chart_type: column
sources:
  - entity: sensor.house_power
    name: Power
    group_by:
      func: avg
      duration: 2h
style:
  chart_options:
    plotOptions:
      bar:
        borderRadius: 6
        columnWidth: "60%"
```

Only plain values work here; ApexCharts options that expect JavaScript functions can't be written in YAML.

---

## A complete example

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
chart_type: area
graph_span: 24h

sources:
  - datasource: living_room
    buffer: smoothed
    name: Temperature
    unit: °C
    float_precision: 1
  - entity: sensor.living_room_humidity
    name: Humidity
    yaxis_id: humidity
    type: line

data_sources:
  living_room:
    entity: sensor.living_room_temperature
    history:
      hours: 24
    processing:
      smoothed:
        type: smooth
        method: exponential
        alpha: 0.2

yaxis:
  - id: temperature
  - id: humidity
    opposite: true
    min: 0
    max: 100

style:
  colors:
    series:
      - "var(--lcars-orange)"
      - "var(--lcars-blue)"
  fill:
    type: gradient
    gradient:
      opacityFrom: 0.5
      opacityTo: 0.05
  legend:
    show: true
  thresholds:
    - value: 22
      label: Warm
      color: var(--lcars-red)
  animation:
    preset: lcars_standard
```
