<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/chart/upgrading.html -->

# Upgrading

## Older chart configs

Earlier versions of the chart card used a different layout for series (`source`, `series_names`, numbered `series_1` data sources, and so on). **You don't need to change anything**: older charts keep working as they are.

What happens with an older chart:

1. **On your dashboard** it is read in the old layout and drawn exactly as before. Nothing is saved or changed.
2. **When you open it in the card editor**, the editor converts it to the current layout and shows a notice saying so. The YAML tab shows the new layout.
   - Press **Save** to keep the converted version.
   - Press **Cancel** to leave your config exactly as it was.
3. **If you type the old layout by hand** in the YAML editor, it still works. The editor shows a warning naming the current option to use, and doesn't rewrite your text while you type.

### What changes

| Older layout | Current layout |
|--------------|----------------|
| `source: sensor.x` with `attribute: a` | `sources: [{ entity: sensor.x, attribute: a }]` |
| `sources: [sensor.x, sensor.y]` | `sources: [{ entity: sensor.x }, { entity: sensor.y }]` |
| `sources: [my_source]` (an LCARdS data source) | `sources: [{ datasource: my_source }]` |
| `series_1`, `series_2`, ... entries the old editor added to `data_sources` | moved into the series as `{ entity: ..., name: ... }` |
| `{ datasource: x, buffer: transformation, key: smooth }` | `{ datasource: x, buffer: smooth }` |
| `series_names: [A, B]` | `name:` on each series |
| `history_hours: 12` (or `history.hours` on a `series_N`) | `graph_span: 12h` |
| `show_legend: true` | `style.legend.show: true` |
| `max_points` | removed: it never had an effect. Use [`group_by`](./series#grouping) |
| `style.grid.opacity` | not an ApexCharts option and never had an effect; use a semi-transparent `style.colors.grid` |

LCARdS data sources you named yourself (anything other than the old editor's `series_1`, `series_2`, ...) are never moved or removed, because other cards may use them too.

### Example

A chart made with the old Chart Studio:

```yaml no-validate
# Before
type: custom:lcards-chart
sources: [series_1]
series_names: [Living room]
data_sources:
  series_1:
    entity: sensor.living_room_temperature
    attribute: state
    history:
      preload: true
      hours: 48
```

```yaml live
# After
type: custom:lcards-chart
graph_span: 48h
sources:
  - entity: sensor.living_room_temperature
    name: Living room
```

To see a conversion explained step by step, pick **Older format (converted)** in the [Playground](./playground).

---

## Coming from apexcharts-card

Many options have the same names as in the popular [apexcharts-card](https://github.com/RomRider/apexcharts-card):

| apexcharts-card | lcards-chart |
|-----------------|--------------|
| `graph_span` | `graph_span` |
| `span.start`, `span.end`, `span.offset` | `span.start`, `span.end`, `span.offset` |
| `series:` | `sources:` |
| `series[].entity`, `attribute` | `sources[].entity`, `attribute` |
| `series[].statistics.type`, `period` | `sources[].statistics.type`, `period` |
| `series[].group_by.func`, `duration`, `fill` | `sources[].group_by.func`, `duration`, `fill` |
| `yaxis[]`, `series[].yaxis_id` | `yaxis[]`, `sources[].yaxis_id` |
| `series[].name`, `unit`, `float_precision`, `curve`, `stroke_width`, `color`, `opacity`, `type` | the same names on `sources[]` |
| `apex_config` | `style.chart_options` |
| `transform`, `data_generator` (JavaScript) | an [LCARdS data source](../../core/datasources/) with processors |

For example, this apexcharts-card config:

```yaml no-validate
type: custom:apexcharts-card
graph_span: 7d
series:
  - entity: sensor.energy_consumption
    statistics:
      type: change
      period: day
```

becomes:

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-chart
chart_type: column
graph_span: 7d
sources:
  - entity: sensor.energy_consumption
    statistics:
      type: change
      period: day
```

---

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/common.html -->

# Common Card Properties

LCARdS share a set of common top-level configuration properties regardless of card type.  This page documents them alongside how sizing interacts with the HA grid system.

## Common Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| `id` | string | Custom card ID for [Rules Engine](../core/rules/) targeting (e.g. `my-light-btn`) |
| `tags` | list | One or more string tags for Rules Engine group targeting (e.g. `[nav, lights]`) |
| `height` | number / string | CSS height override applied to the card host element (see below) |
| `width` | number / string | CSS width override applied to the card host element (see below) |
| `min_height` | number / string | Minimum height floor: card will not shrink below this value (see below) |
| `min_width` | number / string | Minimum width floor: card will not shrink below this value (see below) |
| `max_height` | number / string | Maximum height ceiling: card will not grow beyond this value (see below) |
| `max_width` | number / string | Maximum width ceiling: card will not grow beyond this value (see below) |
| `overflow` | string | CSS overflow shorthand for both axes: `visible`, `hidden`, `clip`, `scroll`, or `auto` |
| `overflow_x` | string | Horizontal axis overflow: same values as `overflow`; overrides the shorthand |
| `overflow_y` | string | Vertical axis overflow: same values as `overflow`; overrides the shorthand |
| `z_index` | integer | CSS z-index on the card host element (range: -999 to 9999) |
| `grid_options` | object | HA grid sizing: `rows` and `columns` for the Lovelace grid (see below) |
| `data_sources` | object | Named data source definitions: see [Data Sources](../core/datasources/) |
| `triggers_update` | list | Extra entity IDs that trigger template re-evaluation; see [Templates](../core/templates/#manual-tracking-with-triggers-update) |
| `preset` | string | Style preset (button, slider, elbow; select menu option buttons): see [Presets](../core/presets.md) |
| `rules` | list | Rules that restyle this or other cards when conditions match: see [Rules Engine](../core/rules/) |
| `animations` | list | Trigger-based animations (on load, on tap, on state change, ...): see [Animations](../core/animations.md) |
| `background_animation` | list | Canvas background effects (button, elbow, slider): see [Background Animations](../core/effects/background-animations.md) |
| `filters` | list | CSS / SVG filters applied to the card: see [Filters](../core/effects/filters.md) |
| `sounds` | object | Per-card sound overrides or `enabled: false`: see [Card Sounds](../core/sounds.md) |
| `variables` | object | Your own named values for templates (see [Variables](#variables-variables) below) |
| `zones` / `debug_zones` | object / boolean | Extra named text zones, and outlines for every zone: see [Text Fields](../core/text-fields.md) |
| `state_attribute` / `ranges_attribute` / `state_classification` | string / string / object | Drive state colours from an attribute or custom buckets: see [Colours](../core/colours.md) |

## Variables (`variables`)

`variables` holds your own named values. Reference them in templates so a value used in several places is set once:

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
entity: light.kitchen
variables:
  accent: "var(--lcars-orange)"
  room: Kitchen
text:
  label:
    content: "{variables.room}"
style:
  card:
    color:
      background:
        active: "[[[ return variables.accent ]]]"
```

Use `{variables.<name>}` in token templates and `variables.<name>` inside `[[[ JavaScript ]]]` templates. See [Templates](../core/templates/).

## Card Identification (`id` and `tags`)

`id` and `tags` are used by the [Rules Engine](../core/rules/) to target cards for conditional style patches.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
id: kitchen-light-btn        # unique identifier - target with rules selector `#kitchen-light-btn`
tags:
  - kitchen
  - lights
  - nav
```

- `id` targets a single specific card (`#kitchen-light-btn`)
- `tags` target groups of cards (`.lights`, `.nav`)
- Neither field affects visual appearance directly: they exist solely for rules targeting and can be helpful with debug logging.

---

## Sizing (`height`, `width`, `min_height`, `min_width`, `max_height`, `max_width`)

### Default behaviour

By default you don't need to set any of these. LCARdS cards are `width: 100%; height: 100%`; they fill whatever grid slot Home Assistant allocates. The card's SVG content automatically scales to fit the available space using a ResizeObserver that measures the rendered container size on every layout change. Use `grid_options` (below) to control how large that slot is.

The four sizing properties are **overrides** for situations where automatic slot-filling isn't sufficient.

### Override formats

All four properties accept the same value formats:

| Value | Result | Example |
|-------|--------|---------|
| Bare integer | Treated as pixels | `200` → `200px` |
| `px` value | Exact pixels | `200px` |
| `vh` / `vw` | Viewport-relative | `50vh` |
| `%` | Percentage of container | `100%` |
| `em` / `rem` | Font-relative | `10em` |

### `height` and `width`

Set an explicit CSS size on the card's host element, overriding whatever the container would normally assign.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
height: 200          # 200px
width: 500px
```

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
height: 50vh         # half viewport height
width: 100%          # fill container
```

### `min_height` and `min_width`

Set a minimum size floor. The card can grow beyond this value but will not shrink below it. Useful when content length is dynamic and you want to prevent the card from collapsing while still allowing it to expand naturally.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
min_height: 40       # never shorter than 40px
min_width: 80        # never narrower than 80px
```

These override the CSS token defaults (`--lcars-button-min-height` and `--lcars-button-min-width`). When `height` is also set, it takes precedence and the `min-height` floor is cleared (`min-height: 0`) so the fixed height is respected exactly. `min_height` and `min_width` do not affect `getCardSize()`.

### `max_height` and `max_width`

Set a maximum size ceiling. The card can shrink below this value but will not grow beyond it. Useful for preventing a card from expanding too far in a flexible or dynamic layout.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
max_height: 200      # never taller than 200px
max_width: 400px     # never wider than 400px
```

Accepts the same formats as `height` and `width` (bare integer = px, or any CSS unit). `max_height` and `max_width` do not affect `getCardSize()`.

### When to use sizing overrides

- **Alert overlays**: explicit size because the overlay container uses `height: auto`
- **Horizontal stacks**: fill remaining space with `width: 100%`
- **Fixed-size panels**: embed a chart or MSD at an exact pixel height
- **Aspect-ratio layouts**: pair `height` with `width` to keep proportions consistent
- **Dynamic content**: use `min_height`/`min_width` to prevent collapse when content length varies

> **Note on `getCardSize()`**: HA uses `getCardSize()` to pre-allocate grid space before the card renders. When `height` is set in pixels, LCARdS uses that value to report grid rows (`px ÷ 56`, rounded up). For non-px units (`vh`, `%`, etc.) the card falls back to its default row count since the pixel value cannot be determined at configuration time.

---

## Overflow (`overflow`, `overflow_x`, `overflow_y`)

Controls what happens when a card's content exceeds its rendered size. Accepts the standard CSS overflow values.

| Value | Behaviour |
|-------|-----------|
| `visible` | Content is not clipped: overflows the card box |
| `hidden` | Content is clipped without a scrollbar |
| `clip` | Like `hidden` but also disallows programmatic scrolling |
| `scroll` | Always shows a scrollbar |
| `auto` | Adds a scrollbar only when content overflows |

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
overflow: hidden        # clip any content that exceeds the card bounds
```

`overflow_x` and `overflow_y` set the horizontal and vertical axes independently and override `overflow` when both are present.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
overflow_x: hidden
overflow_y: auto        # vertical scrollbar only when needed
```

---

## Stacking (`z_index`)

Sets the CSS `z-index` on the card's host element, controlling its stacking order relative to adjacent cards in the same grid container. Useful when cards overlap: for example, an alert overlay, a floating panel, or an MSD embed.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
z_index: 10     # render above neighbouring cards (range: -999 to 9999)
```

---

## HA Grid Sizing (`grid_options`)

`grid_options` controls how the card occupies the Lovelace grid. This is the standard HA mechanism and is independent of `height`/`width`.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-button
grid_options:
  columns: 6    # span 6 grid columns (out of 12)
  rows: 2       # request 2 grid rows of height
```

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `columns` | number | Grid columns to span (HA grid is 12 columns wide) |
| `rows` | number | Grid rows to request |

### `height`/`width`/`min_height`/`min_width` vs `grid_options`

These two systems operate independently and serve different purposes:

| | `height` / `width` / `min_height` / `min_width` | `grid_options` |
|---|---|---|
| **What it sets** | CSS size of the card host element | HA grid slot allocation |
| **Effect on layout** | How large the card *renders* inside its slot | How large a *slot* HA reserves in the grid |
| **Typical use** | Overlays, stacks, fixed-px sizing, dynamic-content floors | Standard dashboard grid layout |
| **Units** | Any CSS unit or bare integer (= px) | Whole numbers only |

In most dashboard layouts you only need `grid_options`. Use the sizing properties when you need to override the rendered size independently of the grid slot, for example when a card is inside a fixed-size container that doesn't use the HA grid.

---

## Sizing inside `custom:layout-card`

Use LCARdS's own [Layout Card](layout-card/) (`custom:lcards-layout-card`) instead of [`custom:layout-card`](https://github.com/thomasloven/lovelace-layout-card). Inside `custom:layout-card`'s grid, LCARdS cards shrink to their minimum height (its grid rows default to `auto` height) and `card_margin` is ignored (the margins are hard-coded). The LCARdS Layout Card has neither problem, and adds the Layout Studio visual editor.

Moving over is a one-line change: set `type: custom:lcards-layout-card` and remove `layout_type`. The `layout` keys and each card's `view_layout` stay the same.

```yaml
type: custom:lcards-layout-card
layout:
  grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr)
  grid-template-rows: 1fr
  height: 300px
cards:
  - type: custom:lcards-button
    preset: lozenge
```

::: details Staying on custom:layout-card?
Add this to the **layout-card itself** (not the LCARdS card) so its rows fill their height:

```yaml
type: custom:layout-card
layout_type: custom:grid-layout
card_mod:
  style: |
    grid-layout {
      --layout-height: 100% !important;
    }
```

`card_margin` stays broken there; the LCARdS Layout Card is the fix.
:::

---

## Card Features

All LCARdS cards support the following cross-cutting features in addition to the common properties above. Each links to the full reference page.

| Feature | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| [Text Labels](../core/text-fields.md) | Multiple positioned text fields with template support, per-field styling, and zone targeting |
| [Actions](../core/actions.md) | `tap_action`, `hold_action`, and `double_tap_action`, any HA action type |
| [Animations](../core/animations.md) | Trigger-based card animations (on load, on state change, etc.) |
| [Background Animations](../core/effects/background-animations.md) | Canvas-rendered animated backgrounds (grid, starfield, fluid, etc.) |
| [Card Sounds](../core/sounds.md) | Per-card audio playback tied to state changes or actions |
| [Rules Engine](../core/rules/) | Conditional style patches driven by entity state, time, or tags |
| [Data Sources](../core/datasources/) | Named entity subscriptions with history buffering and processing |
| [Templates](../core/templates/) | JS, token, DataSource, and Jinja2 template evaluation in any string field |
| [Themes](../core/themes/) | Design token system: colours, typography, borders, and component defaults |

::: tip Not every card supports every feature
Some features are card-specific; for example, `background_animation` is only available on cards that render a canvas layer (Button, Elbow, Slider). Check the individual card page for which features apply.
:::

---

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/data-grid/ -->

# Data Grid Card

`custom:lcards-data-grid`

![Data grid card: LCARS data cascade](/img/lcards-data-grid.gif)

A grid of cells in the LCARS style. Use it two ways:

- **Decorative:** columns of generated numbers and codes, often with the classic LCARS colour cascade rolling down the rows. No entities needed.
- **Data:** a table you write yourself, where each cell is text, a live entity state or a template.

::: tip Try it
- In the card editor, **Open Configuration Studio** gives you a live preview, a spreadsheet of your cells, and row, column and cell styling.
- The [Playground](./playground) lets you edit data grid YAML right here in the docs and see the result.
:::

The grids on these pages are live previews drawn by the card's own code. Entities show sample values.

| Page | Covers |
|------|--------|
| [Data & Cells](./data) | Rows, cell types, entities and templates, header rows, conditional colours, tap actions |
| [Styling & Animation](./styling) | Style layers, grid layout, the cascade, highlighting changes, filters |
| [Playground](./playground) | Edit YAML and see the grid live |
| [Upgrading](./upgrading) | Older data grid configs and what they become |

---

## Quick start

The decorative grid the card picker adds: six rows of mixed values with the colour cascade.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-data-grid
data_mode: decorative
format: mixed
grid:
  grid-template-rows: repeat(6, auto)
  grid-template-columns: repeat(6, minmax(60px, 1fr))
  gap: 0px
style:
  padding: 0px
  font_size: 22px
animations:
  - trigger: on_load
    preset: cascade-color
```

A small status table. The first row is a header; the middle column shows each entity's state; the last column is a template.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-data-grid
data_mode: data
rows:
  - values: [System, Value, Status]
    header: true
  - [Inside, sensor.living_room_temperature, "{{ 'WARM' if states('sensor.living_room_temperature') | float > 22 else 'OK' }}"]
  - [Outside, sensor.outdoor_temperature, "{{ 'WARM' if states('sensor.outdoor_temperature') | float > 22 else 'OK' }}"]
  - [Humidity, sensor.living_room_humidity, "{{ states('sensor.living_room_humidity') | int }}%"]
grid:
  grid-template-columns: 140px 1fr 90px
  gap: 4px
style:
  font_size: 18px
columns:
  - style:
      align: left
      color: var(--lcars-orange)
```

---

## Which mode should I use?

| | Decorative | Data |
|---|---|---|
| **Shows** | Generated values: digits, decimals, letters or hex | Your rows: text, entity states, templates, data source values |
| **Set up with** | `format`, the grid size in `grid` | `rows` |
| **Changes when** | Every `refresh_interval` ms (optional) | An entity, template or data source changes |
| **Good for** | Filling space with LCARS texture, backgrounds behind other cards | Status panels, sensor tables, system readouts |

`data_mode` picks the mode. When it is left out, a card with `rows` is a data grid and anything else is decorative.

---

## Decorative mode

The grid size comes from the CSS Grid templates: `repeat(6, auto)` rows and `repeat(8, 1fr)` columns give a 6 x 8 grid. Without templates the grid is 8 rows by 12 columns.

| Option | Default | Description |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| `format` | `mixed` | `digit` (0042), `float` (42.17), `alpha` (AB), `hex` (A3F1) or `mixed` |
| `refresh_interval` | `0` | Make new values every this many milliseconds. `0` keeps them fixed. |
| `refresh_cells` | `1` | How much of the grid changes on each refresh: `1` is every cell, `0.2` a fifth of them. Small values look like data trickling in. |
| `columns[].format` | - | A different format for one column, by position |

Here only some of the hex cells change every 1.5 seconds, the first two columns are digits, and changed cells pulse:

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-data-grid
data_mode: decorative
format: hex
refresh_interval: 1500
refresh_cells: 0.15
grid:
  grid-template-rows: repeat(5, auto)
  grid-template-columns: repeat(8, 1fr)
  gap: 0px
columns:
  - format: digit
  - format: digit
style:
  font_size: 20px
  color: var(--lcars-orange)
highlight_changes:
  preset: pulse
  duration: 400
```

Values don't change in the card picker preview, so the picker stays calm.

---

## Configuration at a glance

```yaml
type: custom:lcards-data-grid
data_mode: data              # decorative | data (default: data when rows are set)

# Data mode: see Data & Cells
rows:
  - values: [SYSTEM, VALUE]
    header: true
  - [CPU, sensor.cpu_usage]
cell_tap_action:             # optional: tapping an entity cell
  action: more-info
data_sources: {}             # optional named data sources for {datasource:...} cells

# Decorative mode
format: mixed
refresh_interval: 0
refresh_cells: 1

# Layout and styling: see Styling & Animation
grid:
  grid-template-columns: 120px 1fr
  gap: 8px
style: {}                    # every cell
header_style: {}             # header rows
columns:                     # by position
  - style: {}
    format: hex              # decorative mode only

# Animation
animations:
  - trigger: on_load
    preset: cascade-color
highlight_changes: true
filters: []
```

## Common properties

These work on every LCARdS card. See [Common Card Properties](../common.md).

| Category | Config keys | Reference |
|----------|-------------|-----------|
| Sizing | `height`, `width`, `min_height`, `min_width`, `max_height`, `max_width` | [Sizing](../common.md#sizing-height-width-min-height-min-width-max-height-max-width) |
| Overflow | `overflow`, `overflow_x`, `overflow_y` | [Overflow](../common.md#overflow-overflow-overflow-x-overflow-y) |
| Stacking | `z_index` | [Stacking](../common.md#stacking-z-index) |
| Identity | `id`, `tags` | [ID & Tags](../common.md#card-identification-id-and-tags) |
| HA grid | `grid_options` | [HA Grid Sizing](../common.md#ha-grid-sizing-grid-options) |
| Data | `data_sources`, `triggers_update` | [Data Sources](../../core/datasources/) |
| Animations | `animations` | [Animations](../../core/animations.md) |
| Rules | via `id` / `tags`; rule `style` patches apply to the grid-wide `style` | [Rules Engine](../../core/rules/) |

---

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/data-grid/data.html -->

# Data & Cells

In data mode you write the grid row by row. Each row is a list of cells, and the card works out what each cell is.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-data-grid
data_mode: data
rows:
  - [Room, Temperature, Humidity]
  - [Living room, sensor.living_room_temperature, sensor.living_room_humidity]
  - [Outside, sensor.outdoor_temperature, sensor.outdoor_humidity]
grid:
  grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr 1fr
style:
  font_size: 18px
```

Rows can have different lengths; the grid is as wide as the longest row.

---

## What a cell can be

| You write | The cell shows |
|-----------|----------------|
| `Living room` | The text as written |
| `sensor.living_room_temperature` | The entity's state, formatted by Home Assistant with its unit (`21.4 °C`, `Open`, `On`) |
| `"{{ states('sensor.x') }} W"` | A Home Assistant template (Jinja2), rendered by Home Assistant |
| `"{datasource:net_tx:.1f} MB/s"` | A value from an LCARdS [data source](../../core/datasources/). With a format (`:.1f`) you get the number only; without one, the value with its unit. |
| `"[[[ return entity.state ]]]"` | A JavaScript template |

Cells update by themselves when their entity, template or data source changes.

::: tip Quotes
Put templates in quotes in YAML: `"{{ ... }}"`. An entity id or plain text needs no quotes.
:::

### Showing an attribute

For an attribute, or when the cell needs more than a value, write the cell as an object:

```yaml
rows:
  - - Uptime
    - entity: sensor.system_monitor
      attribute: hours
```

| Cell key | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `value` | What the cell shows: text, an entity id or a template |
| `entity` | Show this entity's state (when `value` is empty), and use it for [conditional colours](#conditional-colours) and [actions](#tap-actions) |
| `attribute` | Show this attribute of `entity` instead of its state |
| `style` | Style for this cell only (see [Styling](./styling#style-layers)) |
| `tap_action`, `hold_action`, `double_tap_action` | Standard Home Assistant actions |

Plain cells and cell objects mix freely in a row.

### Data sources

A data source can smooth, scale or convert a sensor before the grid shows it. Define it under `data_sources` and refer to it by name:

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-data-grid
data_mode: data
data_sources:
  power:
    entity: sensor.kitchen_power
rows:
  - [Kitchen, "{datasource:power:.0f} W"]
grid:
  grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr
style:
  font_size: 20px
```

See [Data Sources](../../core/datasources/) for processing options.

---

## Header rows

Write a row as `{ values: [...] }` to give it options. `header: true` makes it a header: bold, uppercase and smaller, with a divider line, in the theme's header colours.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-data-grid
data_mode: data
rows:
  - values: [Deck, Section, Status]
    header: true
  - [Deck 1, Bridge, Nominal]
  - [Deck 5, Sickbay, Nominal]
  - values: [Engineering]
    header: true
  - [Deck 12, Warp core, Online]
grid:
  grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr 1fr
style:
  font_size: 18px
header_style:
  color: var(--lcars-orange)
```

Any number of rows can be headers. Change their look for the whole grid with `header_style` ([Styling](./styling#header-rows)), or for one row with that row's `style`.

---

## Conditional colours

A cell's `color` or `background` can change with the state of the cell's entity, using the same state map as other LCARdS cards:

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-data-grid
data_mode: data
rows:
  - values: [Load, Watts]
    header: true
  - - Kitchen
    - value: sensor.kitchen_power
      style:
        color:
          default: var(--lcars-green)
          above:400: var(--lcars-yellow)
          above:800: var(--lcars-red)
  - - Phone battery
    - value: sensor.phone_battery
      style:
        background:
          default: transparent
          below:30: var(--lcars-red)
grid:
  grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr
style:
  font_size: 20px
```

The cell's entity is its `entity`, or the `value` when that is an entity id. Keys you can use:

| Key | Matches when the entity state |
|-----|-------------------------------|
| `on`, `off`, `open`, `heat`, ... | is exactly that state |
| `above:N`, `below:N`, `at_least:N`, `at_most:N` | is a number past N (the closest match wins) |
| `between:A:B` | is a number from A to B |
| `zero`, `non_zero` | is 0, or any other number |
| `active`, `inactive`, `unavailable` | is on/off style active, inactive, or unavailable/unknown |
| `default` | none of the above |

For a template cell, add `entity:` to say which entity the colours follow. Cells without an entity use `default`.

State maps work on row, column and grid-wide styles too; they resolve against each cell's own entity. See [Colours](../../core/colours.md) for every colour format.

::: info With the cascade
A running cascade animates the text colour of every cell, so text-colour state maps only show when there is no cascade. Background state maps always show.
:::

---

## Tap actions

Cells do nothing when tapped unless you ask. Two ways:

- **`cell_tap_action`** for every entity cell. The most common choice is `more-info`, which opens the entity's dialog:

  ```yaml
  cell_tap_action:
    action: more-info
  ```

- **`tap_action`, `hold_action` or `double_tap_action`** on a cell object, for that cell only. These override `cell_tap_action`.

  ```yaml
  - value: light.kitchen
    tap_action:
      action: toggle
  ```

Actions use the cell's entity by default, and take every standard [action](../../core/actions.md). Cells with an action show a pointer cursor.

---

## In the Configuration Studio

The **Grid Structure** tab shows your rows as a spreadsheet:

- Click a **cell** to choose Entity (with an optional attribute) or Text or template, and to set the cell's style, conditional colours and actions.
- Click a **row** or **column** header to insert, move or delete it, set its style, or mark a row as a header.
- **Add Row** and **Add Column** grow the grid. Custom column widths such as `100px 1fr 80px` are kept when you add, move or remove columns.

Saving keeps your YAML short: rows without options stay plain lists, and cells without options stay plain values.

---

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/data-grid/playground.html -->

# Data Grid Playground

Edit the YAML and the grid redraws as you type. Pick a starting point from the list, or paste a grid from your own dashboard.

**You don't need to know the YAML to start:**

- **Quick settings** above the editor change the most common options for you.
- **Type in the editor** and it suggests the options that fit where your cursor is, with a short description. Press **Ctrl+Space** to see suggestions anywhere, and hover over a key to read what it does.
- **Options here** (under the editor) lists everything you can add at the cursor. **Insert** adds it at the right indent, and **Docs** opens its section in a new tab.

<ClientOnly>

</ClientOnly>

## How the preview works

The preview uses the data grid card's own code: the same rows and cells, style layers, grid layout, decorative values, cascade timing, animation presets and validation as on your dashboard. The docs site has no Home Assistant, so:

- **Entities get sample values.** Names containing `temperature`, `humidity`, `power`, `energy` or `battery` get a realistic value with a unit, and `light.*`/`switch.*`/`binary_sensor.*` entities are on or off. Any other entity gets a plain number.
- **Templates** show sample values for simple forms: `states('...')` with `float`, `int` or `round`, `state_attr(...)`, a one-line `'A' if ... > N else 'B'`, and `{datasource:...}`. Anything else shows an ellipsis. On a dashboard, Home Assistant renders them all.
- **Tap actions** say what they would do instead of doing it.
- **`theme:` tokens** use the default LCARdS theme.

Messages under the grid show schema warnings, and explain how an [older format](./upgrading) would be converted.

When it looks right, **Copy YAML** and paste it into your card's YAML editor, then swap in your own entities.

---

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/data-grid/styling.html -->

# Styling & Animation

## Style layers

Every cell gets its style from up to six layers. Later layers win, key by key:

| Order | Layer | Applies to |
|-------|-------|------------|
| 1 | Theme defaults | Every cell: theme text colour, right-aligned, 24px Antonio |
| 2 | `style` | Every cell |
| 3 | Header defaults, then `header_style` | Rows with `header: true` |
| 4 | `columns[i].style` | Column i (counting from 0) |
| 5 | Row `style` | One row (`{ values: [...], style: {...} }`) |
| 6 | Cell `style` | One cell (a [cell object](./data#showing-an-attribute)) |

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-data-grid
data_mode: data
rows:
  - values: [Sensor, Reading]
    header: true
  - [Inside, sensor.living_room_temperature]
  - values: [Outside, sensor.outdoor_temperature]
    style:
      background: var(--lcars-blue)
  - - Battery
    - value: sensor.phone_battery
      style:
        color: var(--lcars-yellow)
        font_weight: 700
grid:
  grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr
style:
  font_size: 18px
  color: var(--lcars-african-violet)
columns:
  - style:
      align: left
header_style:
  color: var(--lcars-orange)
```

Rule patches from the [rules engine](../../core/rules/) apply to the grid-wide `style`.

### Style keys

Every layer takes the same keys. Numbers become pixels, except `font_weight` and `line_height`.

| Key | Example | Description |
|-----|---------|-------------|
| `color` | `var(--lcars-orange)` | Text colour, or a [state map](./data#conditional-colours) |
| `background` | `transparent` | Background colour, or a state map |
| `font_size` | `18` or `1.2rem` | Font size |
| `font_family` | `Antonio, sans-serif` | Font |
| `font_weight` | `700` or `bold` | Weight |
| `align` | `left` | Horizontal alignment: `left`, `center`, `right` (default `right`) |
| `align_items` | `flex-start` | Vertical alignment inside the cell |
| `padding` | `4px 8px` | Space inside the cell (default `4px`) |
| `text_transform` | `uppercase` | `none`, `uppercase`, `lowercase`, `capitalize` |
| `letter_spacing` | `0.05em` | Letter spacing |
| `line_height` | `1.2` | Line height |
| `white_space` | `normal` | `nowrap` (default) cuts long text with an ellipsis; `normal`, `pre-wrap` or `pre-line` wrap it |
| `border_width`, `border_color`, `border_style` | `1`, `var(--lcars-gray)`, `solid` | Cell border |
| `border_radius` | `4` | Rounded corners |

Any other CSS property works too, written in snake_case: `border_bottom_color`, `opacity`, `text_shadow`, and so on.

Colours accept everything in [Colours](../../core/colours.md): `var(--lcars-...)`, hex, `theme:` tokens and computed colours such as `alpha(var(--lcars-orange), 0.2)`.

### Header rows

Header rows start from the theme's header look (bold, uppercase, 16px, a 2px divider underneath) before `header_style` applies. To drop the divider:

```yaml
header_style:
  border_bottom_width: 0
```

---

## Grid layout

`grid` takes [CSS Grid](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_grid_layout) properties for the grid container. Column widths are the usual place to start:

| Property | Example | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `grid-template-columns` | `120px 1fr 80px` | Column widths. Default: equal columns. In decorative mode this also sets the number of columns. |
| `grid-template-rows` | `repeat(8, auto)` | Row heights. In decorative mode this also sets the number of rows. |
| `gap` | `8px` | Space between cells (default `8px`) |
| `row-gap`, `column-gap` | `2px` | Space between rows, or columns, only |
| `justify-items`, `align-items` | `center` | Where cells sit inside their grid area |
| `justify-content`, `align-content` | `space-between` | Where the whole grid sits inside the card |
| `grid-auto-flow` | `column` | Fill order |
| `grid-auto-rows`, `grid-auto-columns` | `40px` | Size of rows or columns beyond the templates |

`repeat(N, size)` and `minmax(min, max)` work as in CSS. Numbers in gaps become pixels.

---

## The cascade

The cascade is the LCARS colour wave that rolls through the rows: each row holds a bright colour, snaps briefly to a dark one, flashes pale and repeats, every row on its own timing. Add it with the `cascade-color` animation preset:

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-data-grid
data_mode: decorative
format: digit
grid:
  grid-template-rows: repeat(8, auto)
  grid-template-columns: repeat(10, 1fr)
  gap: 0px
style:
  font_size: 18px
animations:
  - trigger: on_load
    preset: cascade-color
    params:
      pattern: niagara
      colors:
        start: var(--lcars-orange)
        text: var(--lcars-red)
        end: var(--lcars-yellow)
```

| Param | Default | Description |
|-------|---------|-------------|
| `pattern` | `default` | Row timing: `default` (the original mixed rhythm), `niagara` (smooth, even), `fast`, or `custom` |
| `speed_multiplier` | `1` | `2` runs twice as fast, `0.5` half as fast |
| `duration` | - | One cycle length in ms for every row (overrides the pattern and `speed_multiplier`) |
| `timing` | - | Per-row timing for `pattern: custom`: a list of `{ duration, delay }` (ms and seconds), repeated for further rows |
| `colors` | theme cascade colours | `{ start, text, end }` (or a list of three): the long bright hold, the short dark snap, the pale flash |
| `ease` | `linear` | Easing between colours |

A custom rhythm:

```yaml
animations:
  - trigger: on_load
    preset: cascade-color
    params:
      pattern: custom
      timing:
        - { duration: 3000, delay: 0.1 }   # row 1
        - { duration: 2000, delay: 0.2 }   # row 2
        - { duration: 4000, delay: 0.3 }   # row 3, then the list repeats
```

The cascade animates the text colour, so cells under a cascade ignore their own text `color` (backgrounds still apply). It works in both modes. Other [animation presets](../../core/animations.md) work on the grid as a whole; to target cells, use selectors such as `.grid-cell[data-row="0"]`.

In the Configuration Studio, the preview leaves animations off until you press the animation button in its toolbar.

---

## Highlighting changes

`highlight_changes` briefly animates cells whose value just changed: an entity update in data mode, or a refresh in decorative mode.

```yaml
highlight_changes: true            # pulse, 500 ms
```

```yaml
highlight_changes:
  preset: glow                     # pulse or glow
  duration: 600
  params:
    color: var(--lcars-orange)
    blur_max: 8
  max_cells: 20                    # at most this many at once (default: all, up to 100)
```

| Option | Default | Description |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| `preset` | `pulse` | Any animation preset; `pulse` and `glow` suit this best |
| `duration` | `500` | Length in ms; the cell animates out and back |
| `ease` | `outQuad` | Easing |
| `params` | - | Preset params, e.g. `max_scale: 1.08` for pulse, `color` and `blur_max` for glow |
| `max_cells` | all (up to 100) | Limit for large grids |

---

## Filters

`filters` applies CSS filters (blur, brightness, hue rotation, ...) to the whole grid. See [Filters](../../core/effects/filters.md); SVG filters don't apply to this card.

```yaml
filters:
  - type: brightness
    value: 0.8
```

---

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/data-grid/upgrading.html -->

# Upgrading

Earlier versions of the data grid used a few different keys: a second `animation:` block next to `animations:`, numeric grid sizes, top-level font settings, and cell styles kept in a separate list. **You don't need to change anything**: older grids keep working.

What happens with an older grid:

1. **On your dashboard** it is converted in memory and drawn as before. Nothing is saved or changed.
2. **When you open it in the card editor**, the editor converts it to the current layout and shows a notice listing what changed. The YAML tab shows the new layout.
   - Press **Save** to keep the converted version.
   - Press **Cancel** to leave your config exactly as it was.
3. **If you type an old key by hand** in the YAML editor, it still works. The editor shows a warning naming the current option to use, and doesn't rewrite your text while you type.

Decorative grids made from the card picker's starting config already use the current layout.

## What changes

| Older layout | Current layout |
|--------------|----------------|
| `data_mode: random` | `data_mode: decorative` |
| `data_mode: template` or `datasource` | `data_mode: data` |
| `grid: { rows: 8, columns: 12 }` | `grid: { grid-template-rows: repeat(8, auto), grid-template-columns: repeat(12, 1fr) }` |
| `grid.cell_width: 80` | `grid-template-columns: repeat(N, 80px)` |
| `font_size`, `font_family`, `font_weight`, `align` at the top level | the same keys inside `style` |
| `animation: { type: cascade, pattern, colors, ... }` | an `animations` entry with `preset: cascade-color` and those settings as `params` |
| `animation.timing` | `params.timing` on the `cascade-color` animation |
| `animation.highlight_changes`, `change_preset`, `change_duration`, `change_easing`, `change_params`, `max_highlight_cells` | `highlight_changes: { preset, duration, ease, params, max_cells }` |
| `rows[].cellStyles` (written by the old Studio) | each cell becomes `{ value, style }` |
| `rows[].sources` | removed: an older format the card no longer read |

Some old settings start working after the upgrade. Top-level `font_size` and `align` were ignored by the cell styles before; inside `style` they apply. A legacy `animation.type: cascade` never started a cascade (it only removed the cell colours); as a `cascade-color` animation it runs.

## Example

```yaml no-validate
# Before
type: custom:lcards-data-grid
data_mode: random
format: digit
grid:
  rows: 4
  columns: 8
font_size: 18
animation:
  type: cascade
  pattern: niagara
  highlight_changes: true
  change_preset: glow
```

```yaml live
# After
type: custom:lcards-data-grid
data_mode: decorative
format: digit
grid:
  grid-template-rows: repeat(4, auto)
  grid-template-columns: repeat(8, 1fr)
style:
  font_size: 18
animations:
  - trigger: on_load
    preset: cascade-color
    params:
      pattern: niagara
highlight_changes:
  preset: glow
```

To see a conversion explained, pick **Older format (converted)** in the [Playground](./playground).

---

<!-- https://lcards.unimatrix01.ca/dev/cards/elbow/ -->

# Elbow Card

`custom:lcards-elbow`

The Elbow card creates the iconic LCARS corner/cap shapes: the L-shaped coloured bars that frame sections of an LCARS interface. Extends the button card so it inherits text, actions, rules, animations, and templates.

---

## Quick Start

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-elbow
elbow:
  type: header-left
  segment:
    bar_width: 90
    bar_height: 20
```

---

## Common Properties

The following properties are shared across all LCARdS cards. See [Common Card Properties](../common.md) for full details.

| Category | Config keys | Reference |
|----------|-------------|-----------|
| Sizing | `height`, `width`, `min_height`, `min_width`, `max_height`, `max_width` | [Sizing](../common.md#sizing-height-width-min-height-min-width-max-height-max-width) |
| Overflow | `overflow`, `overflow_x`, `overflow_y` | [Overflow](../common.md#overflow-overflow-overflow-x-overflow-y) |
| Stacking | `z_index` | [Stacking](../common.md#stacking-z-index) |
| Identity | `id`, `tags` | [ID & Tags](../common.md#card-identification-id-and-tags) |
| HA Grid | `grid_options` | [HA Grid Sizing](../common.md#ha-grid-sizing-grid-options) |
| Data | `data_sources`, `triggers_update` | [Data Sources](../../core/datasources/) |
| Text labels | `text` | [Text Fields](../../core/text-fields.md) |
| Actions | `tap_action`, `hold_action`, `double_tap_action` | [Actions](../../core/actions.md) |
| Animations | `animations`, `background_animation` | [Animations](../../core/animations.md) |
| Sounds | `sounds` | [Sounds](../../core/sounds.md) |
| Rules | via `id` / `tags` | [Rules Engine](../../core/rules/) |

---

## Config Structure

Annotated map of all top-level keys. The most important key is `elbow`; everything else is optional.

```yaml
type: custom:lcards-elbow

# ── Elbow geometry ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
elbow:
  type: header-left     # header-left | header-right | footer-left | footer-right
                        # header-contained | header-open | footer-open | footer-contained
                        # diagonal-cap-left | diagonal-cap-right | frame
  style: simple         # simple (default) | segmented
  segment:              # for simple style
    bar_width: 90       # vertical bar thickness in px ('theme' for HA-LCARS binding)
    bar_height: 20      # horizontal bar thickness in px
    outer_curve: auto   # arc radius keyword - see Arc Radius Modes below
    color:              # string or state-based object
      default: "var(--lcars-orange)"
      inactive: "alpha(var(--lcars-orange), 0.3)"
  segments:             # for segmented style
    gap: 4
    outer_segment:
      bar_width: 90
      color:            # string or state-based object
        default: "var(--lcars-orange)"
    inner_segment:
      bar_width: 30
      color:            # string or state-based object
        default: "var(--lcards-moonlight)"

# ── Identity & entity ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
entity: light.living_room  # entity for state-based colouring
id: my-elbow               # rules engine targeting
tags: [nav]                # group tags

# ── Appearance ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ranges_attribute: ""      # entity attribute for range conditions
shape_texture:
  preset: fluid            # Canvas2D texture clipped to the elbow fill
filters: []               # CSS / SVG filters

# ── Text, actions & animations ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
text:
  label:
    content: NAVIGATION
    position: top-right
tap_action:
  action: toggle
animations: []
background_animation:
  inset: auto              # sizes canvas to the open content area
  effects: []              # stack of background effects rendered bottom → top
sounds: {}

# ── Layout ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
height: 200
width: 300
min_height: 100
max_height: 400
overflow: hidden
z_index: 0
grid_options:
  columns: 6
  rows: 4
data_sources: {}
triggers_update: []
```

---

## Card Options

| Option | Type | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `type` | string | `custom:lcards-elbow` (required) |
| `elbow` | object | Elbow geometry and styling: see [Elbow Types](#elbow-types) (required) |
| `entity` | string | Entity to monitor for state-based styling |
| `preset` | string | Optional button-style preset base (e.g. `lozenge`, `pill`) |
| `ranges_attribute` | string | Entity attribute for range conditions: see [Range Conditions](../../core/colours.md#range-conditions-on-non-numeric-entities-ranges-attribute) |
| `state_attribute` | string | Attribute whose string value drives exact-key colour matching; see [state_attribute](../../core/colours.md#exact-match-keys-from-an-attribute-state-attribute) |
| `shape_texture` | object | Canvas2D texture inside the elbow shape fill: see [Button card → Shape Texture](../button/#shape-texture) |
| `filters` | list | Visual filters (CSS / SVG filter primitives); see [Filters](../../core/effects/filters.md) |

---

## Elbow Types

Set via `elbow.type`. The type determines the corner position and shape of the L-bar.

| Type | Description | Styles |
|------|-------------|--------|
| `header-left` | Top-left corner: vertical bar on left, horizontal bar on top | simple, segmented |
| `header-right` | Top-right corner: vertical bar on right, horizontal bar on top | simple, segmented |
| `footer-left` | Bottom-left corner: vertical bar on left, horizontal bar on bottom | simple, segmented |
| `footer-right` | Bottom-right corner: vertical bar on right, horizontal bar on bottom | simple, segmented |
| `header-contained` | Horizontal bar with mirrored elbows on both left and right ends (top) | simple |
| `footer-contained` | Horizontal bar with mirrored elbows on both left and right ends (bottom) | simple |
| `header-open` | Simple horizontal bar at top: no vertical arms | simple |
| `footer-open` | Simple horizontal bar at bottom: no vertical arms | simple |
| `diagonal-cap-left` | Top-left with configurable diagonal cut on both corners (controlled by `segment.diagonal_angle`) | simple, segmented |
| `diagonal-cap-right` | Top-right with configurable diagonal cut on both corners | simple, segmented |
| `diagonal-cap-footer-left` | Bottom-left with configurable diagonal cut on both corners | simple, segmented |
| `diagonal-cap-footer-right` | Bottom-right with configurable diagonal cut on both corners | simple, segmented |
| `bar-slant-right` | A straight bar (the whole card) with a slanted right end; the slant follows `segment.diagonal_angle` | simple |
| `bar-slant-left` | The same, slanted on the left | simple |
| `bar-parallelogram` | Both ends slanted the same way | simple |
| `frame` | Full rectangular frame: 2–4 sided border with per-side widths and per-corner radii | simple, segmented |

Every type, rendered:

---

## Elbow Styles

### Simple (default)

Single elbow: one curved L-shape.

```yaml
elbow:
  type: header-left
  style: simple
  segment:
    bar_width: 90       # Vertical bar thickness (px)
    bar_height: 20      # Horizontal bar thickness (px)
    outer_curve: auto   # arc radius keyword - see Arc Radius Modes below
    color:
      default: "var(--lcards-orange)"
      active: "var(--lcards-orange-medium)"
```

### Segmented (TNG / Picard style)

Two concentric elbows with a gap: the double-elbow look from Star Trek TNG.

```yaml
elbow:
  type: header-left
  style: segmented
  segments:
    gap: 4
    outer_segment:
      bar_width: 90
      bar_height: 20
      color: "var(--lcars-orange)"
    inner_segment:
      bar_width: 30
      bar_height: 10
      color: "var(--lcards-moonlight)"
```

Both styles side by side:

---

## Segment Options (Simple Style)

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|--------|------|---------|-------------|
| `bar_width` | number / `"theme"` | `90` | Vertical bar thickness in px. Use `"theme"` to bind to `input_number.lcars_vertical` |
| `bar_height` | number / `"theme"` | `20` | Horizontal bar thickness in px. Use `"theme"` to bind to `input_number.lcars_horizontal` |
| `outer_curve` | number / keyword | `"auto"` | Corner arc radius. See [Arc Radius Modes](#arc-radius-modes). |
| `outer_curve_clamp` | `"card"` / `"none"` / number | `"card"` | Clamp behaviour. `"card"` = `min(card_w, card_h)` (default). `"none"` = no clamp (fix for paired elbow inconsistency). number = explicit px ceiling. |
| `inner_curve` | number / keyword | - | Inner arc radius. Same keywords as `outer_curve` plus `"auto"` = `outer_curve / 2` (LCARS formula, default when omitted). |
| `diagonal_angle` | number / `"theme"` | `45` | Cut angle in degrees for the diagonal-cap and bar-slant types (90 = square). Use `"theme"` to bind to `input_number.lcars_elbow_angle` |
| `color` | string / object | - | Fill colour: [state map](../../core/colours.md) supported |

---

## Arc Radius Modes

The `outer_curve` property accepts either an explicit pixel value or a keyword that derives the radius from the arm dimensions. The render engine clamps the result to `min(card_width, card_height)` to keep arc tangent points within the card viewport.

| Keyword | Formula | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `"auto"` / `"arm_width"` | `bar_width / 2` | LCARS classic default. Arc sweeps through the vertical arm. |
| `"arm_height"` | `bar_height / 2` | Arc based on horizontal arm. Tiny with thin horizontal bars. |
| `"arm_max"` | `max(bar_width, bar_height) / 2` | **Recommended for paired elbows.** Uses the larger arm; equals `auto` for typical LCARS configs (wide vertical bar, thin horizontal bar), but self-corrects when orientation is reversed. |
| `"arm_min"` | `min(bar_width, bar_height) / 2` | Based on the thinner arm. Very small with asymmetric bars. Useful for compact corners. |
| `"arm_fill"` | `max(bar_width, bar_height)` | Maximum sweeping arc: fills the entire dominant arm. Dramatic effect. |
| number | explicit px | Set the radius directly in pixels. |

Each mode with a 90 px wide vertical arm and a 24 px horizontal arm:

**Tangent geometry:** Arcs always arrive at exactly 0° (tangent) to their edges, a property of the quarter-circle shape. The mode controls *where on the edge* the tangent point lands, not the arrival angle.

**Why paired elbows look different with `auto`:** The render-time viewport clamp reduces the radius when `outer_curve` exceeds the card height. Two elbows in differently-sized cards get different clamped radii. Fix: set `outer_curve_clamp: none` to decouple the radius from card height entirely.

**`inner_curve` keywords:** `inner_curve` accepts the same keyword set. `"auto"` (default) uses `outer_curve / 2`. The keywords derive the inner radius independently from bar dimensions, letting you decouple inner from outer (e.g. `outer_curve: arm_max, inner_curve: arm_height` for an asymmetric corner feel).

**Paired elbows: the correct config** (issue #361 fix):

```yaml
# Both elbows identical - outer_curve_clamp: none prevents card height from affecting radius
elbow:
  type: header-left
  segment:
    bar_width: 130
    bar_height: 15
    outer_curve: arm_max        # max(130,15)/2 = 65px sweeping arc
    outer_curve_clamp: none     # no card-height clamping - consistent in any layout
```

```yaml
elbow:
  type: footer-left
  segment:
    bar_width: 130
    bar_height: 15
    outer_curve: arm_max
    outer_curve_clamp: none
```

---

## Segments Options (Segmented Style)

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|--------|------|---------|-------------|
| `gap` | number | `4` | Gap in px between outer and inner elbow |
| `outer_segment` | object | - | Outer (frame) segment config: see below |
| `inner_segment` | object | - | Inner (content) segment config: see below |

### `outer_segment` and `inner_segment` fields

Both `outer_segment` and `inner_segment` share the same schema:

| Option | Type | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `bar_width` | number | Vertical bar thickness in px (**required**) |
| `bar_height` | number | Horizontal bar thickness in px (defaults to `bar_width`) |
| `outer_curve` | number / keyword | Outer corner radius: same keyword modes as simple style |
| `outer_curve_clamp` | `"card"` / `"none"` / number | Clamp behaviour: same as simple style |
| `inner_curve` | number / keyword | Inner arc radius: same keyword modes as simple style (`"auto"` = `outer_curve / 2`) |
| `diagonal_angle` | number / `"theme"` | Diagonal cut angle in degrees (diagonal-cap types only). Use `"theme"` to bind to `input_number.lcars_elbow_angle`. Default: `45` |
| `color` | string / object | Fill colour: [state map](../../core/colours.md) supported |
| `entity_id` | string | Entity ID for state-based colour on this segment |
| `tap_action` | object | Tap action for this segment: see [Actions](../../core/actions.md) |
| `hold_action` | object | Hold action for this segment |
| `double_tap_action` | object | Double-tap action for this segment |

---

## Frame Type

`type: frame` draws a rectangular border around the card instead of an L-shape. Each side can be switched off (an open side ends in rounded caps) or given its own thickness, and each corner its own curves. Set the sizes under `elbow.frame`; the colour comes from `elbow.segment.color`, as for every elbow.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-elbow
grid_options:
  rows: 4
elbow:
  type: frame
  segment:
    color: "var(--lcards-orange)"
  frame:
    bar_width: 40       # left and right sides
    bar_height: 16      # top and bottom
    right:
      enabled: false    # open on the right
    corners:
      top_left:
        outer_curve: 40
```

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|--------|------|---------|-------------|
| `bar_width` | number / string | `90` | Thickness of the left and right sides (a number is px) |
| `bar_height` | number / string | `bar_width` | Thickness of the top and bottom sides |
| `outer_curve` | number / string | half of `bar_width` | Outer radius of every corner |
| `inner_curve` | number / string | half of `outer_curve` | Inner radius of every corner |
| `top`, `bottom`, `left`, `right` | object | - | One side: `enabled` (default `true`), and a thickness as `bar_width`, `bar_height` or `thickness` |
| `corners` | object | - | One corner each (`top_left`, `top_right`, `bottom_left`, `bottom_right`): `outer_curve`, `inner_curve` |
| `segments` | object | - | `style: segmented` only: a second ring inside the first, see below |

### Segmented frame

With `style: segmented`, `frame.segments` adds an inner ring: `gap` is the space between the rings (default `4`), and `inner_frame` takes the same keys as `frame` (its `bar_width` defaults to `28`) plus its own `color` (default: the outer ring's colour; state maps work).

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-elbow
grid_options:
  rows: 4
elbow:
  type: frame
  style: segmented
  segment:
    color: "var(--lcards-orange)"
  frame:
    bar_width: 30
    segments:
      gap: 6
      inner_frame:
        bar_width: 10
        color: "var(--lcards-moonlight)"
```

---

## HA-LCARS Theme Binding

If you use the [HA-LCARS theme](https://github.com/th3jesta/ha-lcars), bind bar dimensions to the theme helpers to keep all elbows synchronised:

```yaml
elbow:
  type: footer-right
  segment:
    bar_width: theme     # Reads input_number.lcars_vertical
    bar_height: theme    # Reads input_number.lcars_horizontal
```

Changing the helper value updates every elbow using `theme` binding simultaneously.

---

## Text Labels

Elbows inherit the full button text system. Common use: a label on the horizontal bar.

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-elbow
elbow:
  type: header-left
  segment:
    bar_width: 120
    bar_height: 22
text:
  section:
    content: NAVIGATION
    position: top-right
    font_size: 11
    font_weight: bold
    color: "var(--lcards-moonlight)"
```

See [Text Fields](../../core/text-fields.md) for the complete reference.

---

## Background Animation Inset

Elbow cards support a canvas-level `inset` on `background_animation` so the animation fills only the open content area, not the LCARS bars.

### Auto inset (recommended)

Use `inset: auto` to let the card automatically derive the correct inset from its bar geometry:

```yaml live
type: custom:lcards-elbow
elbow:
  type: header-left
  segment:
    bar_width: 90
    bar_height: 20
background_animation:
  inset: auto       # canvas sized to avoid the elbow bars
  effects:
    - preset: grid
      config:
        line_spacing: 40
        color: "alpha(var(--lcards-orange), 0.3)"
```

### Manual inset

Supply explicit pixel values when you need precise control:

```yaml
background_animation:
  inset:
    top: 20         # height of horizontal top bar
    left: 90        # width of vertical left bar
    right: 0
    bottom: 0
  effects:
    - preset: starfield
      config:
        count: 150
```

> **Note**: `inset: auto` is computed from the resolved bar geometry at runtime and updates automatically when theme bar dimensions change via `input_number` helpers.

---

## Shape Texture

Elbow cards support the same `shape_texture` feature as button cards: a Canvas2D texture or animation clipped to the elbow shape fill (simple and segmented styles). Configuration is identical.

See [Button card: Shape Texture](../button/#shape-texture) for the full preset reference and examples.

---

## Symbiont

The Symbiont feature embeds any Home Assistant card inside the elbow's content area. LCARdS mounts the card in the open frame and can optionally inject styles directly into the embedded card's shadow root ("imprinting"), keeping the look consistent with your LCARS theme without modifying the embedded card's own config.

### Basic Example

```yaml
type: custom:lcards-elbow
elbow:
  type: header-left
  segment:
    bar_width: 100
    bar_height: 22
symbiont:
  enabled: true
  card:
    type: alarm-panel
    entity: alarm_control_panel.home
    states:
      - arm_away
      - arm_home
```

### Symbiont Options

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|--------|------|---------|-------------|
| `enabled` | boolean | `false` | Enable or disable the symbiont |
| `overflow` | string | `hidden` | CSS overflow for both axes of the symbiont container: `visible`, `hidden`, `clip`, `scroll`, `auto` |
| `overflow_x` | string | - | CSS overflow-x (horizontal). Overrides `overflow` shorthand |
| `overflow_y` | string | - | CSS overflow-y (vertical). Overrides `overflow` shorthand |
| `card` | object | - | Any valid HA card config (`type` + card properties) |
| `position` | object | - | Padding (px) within the elbow content area |
| `position.top` | number | `10` | Top padding |
| `position.left` | number | `10` | Left padding |
| `position.right` | number | `10` | Right padding |
| `position.bottom` | number | `0` | Bottom padding |
| `size` | object | - | Explicit dimensions for the symbiont container. If omitted, the container fills the full inset area |
| `size.width` | string | - | CSS width (e.g. `"95%"`, `"300px"`, `"clamp(200px, 80%, 600px)"`) |
| `size.height` | string | - | CSS height |
| `anchor` | string | `top-left` | Alignment of the sized container within the inset area. Only applies when `size` is set. Options: `top-left`, `top-center`, `top-right`, `middle-left`, `center`, `middle-right`, `bottom-left`, `bottom-center`, `bottom-right` |
| `imprint` | object | - | Shadow-root style injection: see below |
| `custom_style` | string | - | Raw CSS appended to the embedded card's shadow root (no UIX required) |

### Size & Anchor

By default the symbiont container fills the entire content area (after `position` padding is applied). Set `size` to constrain it to explicit dimensions, then use `anchor` to control where it sits within that area.

```yaml
symbiont:
  enabled: true
  position:
    top: 10
    right: 10
    bottom: 10
    left: 10
  size:
    width: "95%"
    height: "95%"
  anchor: center
  card:
    type: entities
    entities:
      - sensor.temperature
```

`anchor` has no effect when `size` is omitted; the container already fills all available space.

### Imprint

Imprint injects a `<style>` element directly into the embedded card's shadow root. Properties are resolved against the elbow's entity state, so they react to state changes exactly like the elbow's own colours.

| Option | Type | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `imprint.enabled` | boolean | `true` by default: set `false` to disable all injection |
| `imprint.background` | string / state map | Background colour injected on `ha-card` |
| `imprint.text.color` | string / state map | Text colour injected on `ha-card` |
| `imprint.text.font_size` | string | Font size (e.g. `"14px"`) |
| `imprint.text.font_family` | string | Font family string |
| `imprint.border_radius` | object | Per-corner border radii: see below |

Colour values accept the same forms as everywhere else in LCARdS: hex, `rgba()`, `var(--token)`, `darken()`/`lighten()`/`alpha()` expressions, and full state maps with `default`/`active`/`inactive`/named-state keys.

#### State-Reactive Imprint

```yaml
symbiont:
  enabled: true
  card:
    type: alarm-panel
    entity: alarm_control_panel.home
  imprint:
    background:
      default: "rgba(0,0,0,0.5)"
      active: "alpha(var(--lcars-red), 0.25)"
    text:
      color:
        default: "var(--lcars-orange)"
        active: "var(--lcars-red)"
    border_radius:
      top_left: match       # copies the elbow inner arc radius
      top_right: 0
      bottom_left: 0
      bottom_right: 0
```

#### Border Radius Options

Each corner accepts one of:

| Value | Effect |
|-------|--------|
| `"match"` | Mirrors the elbow's inner arc radius (recommended for the corner adjacent to the elbow) |
| number | Fixed radius in px |
| *(absent)* | Not injected: card keeps its own radius |

The legacy shorthand `imprint.border_radius.match_host: true` (default when `border_radius` is omitted) automatically applies `match` to only the single corner that is adjacent to the elbow hull, leaving the other three corners at `0`. Set to `false` to suppress all radius injection.

### Custom Style

`custom_style` lets you inject arbitrary CSS into the embedded card's shadow root without UIX:

```yaml
symbiont:
  enabled: true
  card:
    type: entities
    entities:
      - sensor.temperature
  custom_style: |
    ha-card {
      --ha-card-border-radius: 0;
      --secondary-text-color: var(--lcards-moonlight);
    }
```

The custom style is appended **after** imprint styles, so it takes precedence when both set the same property.

### Using UIX with Symbiont

[UIX](https://github.com/Lint-Free-Technology/uix) (UI eXtension, which HA-LCARS uses) works with symbiont cards. Put the `uix` block in the embedded card's config; LCARdS passes it straight through. An older `card_mod` block is passed through too, and UIX reads it, but card-mod itself no longer works with current Home Assistant.

**Order:** the embedded card's UIX styles are applied first, then the LCARdS imprint (and `custom_style`) adds `<style id="lcards-symbiont-imprint">` after them. So **imprint wins when both set the same property**; properties only one of them sets don't conflict. To let UIX style the card on its own, turn imprint off with `imprint.enabled: false` (that also turns off `custom_style`).

```yaml
symbiont:
  enabled: true
  card:
    type: alarm-panel
    entity: alarm_control_panel.home
    uix:
      style: |
        ha-card {
          background: transparent !important;
          box-shadow: none !important;
          border: 1px solid var(--lcars-blue, #93e1ff) !important;
          border-radius: 0 !important;
        }
  imprint:
    text:
      color:
        default: "var(--lcars-orange)"
        active: "var(--lcars-red)"
```

> **Note:** `custom_style` injects raw CSS without UIX. For simple shadow-root overrides prefer `custom_style`: it needs nothing else installed and is handled entirely by LCARdS.

### Lazy-Loaded HA Card Types

HA lazy-loads many of its own built-in card modules (e.g. `alarm-panel`, `thermostat`, `media-player`); they are only imported when they first appear on a dashboard. On a fresh page load, before another dashboard view has triggered the import, the element is not yet registered.

LCARdS handles this automatically: when the requested type is not yet registered, it routes through HA's internal `hui-card` wrapper which triggers the correct dynamic import. The card renders as soon as HA finishes loading the module, no configuration required.

---
